---
title: Mobile and desktop apps
description: How to use Hypertask on Android and iPhone, and what to use on Windows and Mac.
---


Hypertask on a phone is the web app at [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai), installed on the device. On a computer, use that same site in a browser, or install it from the browser.

## Is there a mobile app?

### Android

The official Android app is a Trusted Web Activity wrapper of [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai). It opens the web app with its own launcher icon, splash screen, and push notifications. The project README says to download the APK from the [Android releases page](https://github.com/hypertask-ai/android/releases).

<Aside type="note">
That releases page is the download location. If no APK is listed there yet, install the web app with Add to Home Screen until a release is published.
</Aside>

### iPhone and other phones

Install the web app with **Add to Home Screen**.

On an iPhone, open [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai) in Safari, tap **Share**, then **Add to Home Screen**. On other phones, use the browser's **Add to Home Screen** or **Install** command.

The site publishes a web app manifest named Hypertask with `display` set to `standalone`, so the home-screen icon opens Hypertask without the browser toolbar. The live manifest is [app.hypertask.ai/manifest.webmanifest](https://app.hypertask.ai/manifest.webmanifest).

## Is there a desktop app for Windows or Mac?

Use the web app in a browser. Chrome and Edge can also install [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai) as an app from the address bar. That installed window is the same web app.

<Aside type="caution" title="No signed desktop download">
Hypertask does not publish a signed desktop installer for Windows or Mac.
</Aside>

[hypertask-desktop](https://github.com/hypertask-ai/hypertask-desktop) is an early-pilot native client written in Rust with GPUI. It covers Inbox, Board, and Task detail, and you build it from source. The repository has no GitHub release and no signed download.

--- title: Images and Attachments description: Send HEIC/HEIF photos, view them everywhere (thumbnails, inline, galleries, lightboxes), force or exempt from preview, and resize images on pages. --- We treat HEIC and HEIF images like any other file: they render consistently across thumbnails, inline previews, galleries, and lightbox views. If a preview isn't suitable, exclude the format from previews or use a low-res fallback. ## Supported formats | Format | Default behavior | |--------|------------------| | HEIC/HEIF | Keep the original for download; the system generates a JPEG copy for previews | | JPEG/PNG/WebP | Render at full quality | ## Viewing HEIC/HEIF 1. Attach a photo from an iPhone or Mac. 2. The platform creates a browser-compatible JPEG copy for previews, while the original HEIC/HEIF is preserved for download. 3. See it in the same places as regular images: - **Attachment thumbnails** below comments and email bubbles - **Inline embed** inside a comment or task description - **Board gallery** or gallery views that show attachments - **Task detail lightbox** with a thumbnail strip at the bottom ## Downloading HEIC/HEIF HEIC and HEIF photos uploaded to tasks and comments retain their original file format in the download. When you click **Download** on an attachment: - The original HEIC/HEIF file is downloaded, preserving the full image quality - Previews across the platform use the generated JPEG copy for faster rendering and broader compatibility This ensures you can access the highest-quality version of your photos while maintaining fast, consistent previews everywhere else. ## Who can download attachments New Only people who can see the parent ticket can download its attachments. Access follows board membership: people who are not the owner, an Admin, or a Member of that board cannot reach downloads. ### How it works - When opening a task or viewing the task detail lightbox, the system checks that you own the board or are an Admin or Member before exposing download URLs. - If you are not on the board, downloads come back as not found. - The board owner, Admins, and Members who can see the ticket can download files. Agents on that board can download too. - This change prevents unauthorized downloads for attachments that originated on private or board-limited tasks. ### What this protects - Attachments stored on private tickets are not reachable by users who should not see that context. - AI-generated task previews now respect the same access gate, ensuring draft images on private tickets are not exposed outside the intended scope. - Regular downloads continue to work as before for anyone with proper ticket visibility. ### When it applies - The board owner, Admins, Members, and AI agents on the board can download its attachments. - People who are not the board owner, an Admin, or a Member cannot reach downloads. A public share link can show the board, and it does not let them download. ## Excluding previews To prevent HEIC/HEIF from generating previews (e.g., if the file is too large for preview generation): 1. Open the attachment's context menu (three dots). 2. Select **Excluded from previews** to disable automatic preview generation. 3. Uploaders still receive the file; observers only see the original format and a download link. ## Lightbox image strip In the task detail lightbox, the thumbnail strip shows all attachments in that task. Supported formats and non-preview status appear consistently across all attachments. ## Handling malformed previews in the lightbox strip If the lightbox shows a broken image icon for a non-decodable file: - A file icon now appears instead of a broken icon, making it clear the image content could not be decoded. ## Warnings for unexpected content If a file exhibits preview or display issues (broken icons, no thumbnail, or an unexpected format shown), check: - The file is flagged as excluded from previews (if the goal was to prevent preview). - The file is a HEIC/HEIF image under preview logic (historically, some browsers rendered these as named files before conversion completed). ## Upload tips - **Keep resolution manageable:** Very large HEIC images can lead to longer preview conversion times. - **Review lightbox strip:** If a thumbnail seems wrong after a HEIC upload, the browser might still be loading a placeholder until conversion finishes. ## Paste support You can paste photos directly into comments and task descriptions. The system handles both HEIC/HEIF files and regular image formats in the same paste handler: - HEIC/HEIF: Preserves the original and generates a JPEG preview - JPEG/PNG/WebP: Downloads as-is This gives you a single paste workflow whether you're uploading from Photos via copy-paste or dragging and dropping files. [Learn more about keyboard shortcuts for superhuman-style snippets in the Superhuman-Style Snippets documentation.](/features/superhuman-snippets/) ## Handling blocked image hosts New If your network or a firewall blocks the image server domain, attachments now retry through the app domain and display instead of staying broken. ### How it works - Images usually load directly from `files.hypertask.app`. - When a request to `files.hypertask.app` fails (for example, due to network restrictions or a firewall), the app retries once through `app.hypertask.ai`. - On successful retry, the image displays in comments, task descriptions, attachments, and the task detail lightbox. - This happens automatically; no configuration is required on your side. - Normal networks that can reach `files.hypertask.app` continue to load images straight from the image server, so performance is unchanged. ### When this helps This change helps users on restrictive networks (including some corporate Wi-Fi and VPNs) where: - The image host is blocked, resulting in broken images or connection errors. - You cannot easily unblock the domain. - You don't have control over network policy. Example scenario: A comment includes an image attachment, but your network blocks `files.hypertask.app`. Previously the image would appear broken. Now the app retries through `app.hypertask.ai`, and the image loads as expected. ### Reloading for browsers that blocked images before If you saw broken images on a previous visit and still use a network that blocks the image server: - Refresh the ticket page and the attachments with retry behavior will load properly. - After the initial load, the images are cached by your browser, so you should not need to re-enter restrictive network conditions to see them. [Learn more about keyboard shortcuts in the Keyboard Shortcuts documentation.](/features/keyboard-shortcuts/) ## Resizing images on pages and ticket descriptions You can manually adjust image size on pages and in ticket descriptions. ### Auto-fit vs manual resize - Auto-fit: Images without a saved size automatically adjust to fit the context (mobile, desktop layout, and container width). - Manual resize: Drag the handle on any image to set a custom width. When you type text nearby and the edit is saved, the new size is persisted. ### Persisted size - After you drag an image's resize handle and see "Saved," the image's width is saved to that page or ticket description. - Reloading the page or ticket keeps the image at the custom size instead of reverting to auto-fit. - Using multiple sizes on the same page works as expected: each one stays where you set it. ### Mobile experience - On mobile, resized images still respect screen width and remain readable. - Auto-fit images respond to pinch-to-zoom; resized images follow the set width. ### Common use cases - Bulleted lists with images: Size images consistently (e.g., 50% width) so they look uniform in lists. - Diagrams on pages: Grow or shrink diagrams on a page to finer steps. - Ticket descriptions: Include screenshots at a consistent scale along with typed text. [Learn more about creating pages in the Pages documentation.](/features/pages/) Fix When uploading a file and immediately saving before the preview appears (for example with keyboard shortcuts or Save & new), the attachment now persists on the task instead of dropping.

--- title: What is Hypertask? description: AI-native project management for teams and AI agents — manage tasks, collaborate in real-time, and connect AI agents with MCP, CLI, and REST APIs. --- # What is Hypertask?
Built with agents first. Hypertask comes with an intelligent co-worker that can read your board, create tasks, and respond to comments—all via Chat, CLI, MCP, or REST. Use built-in or programmatic auth. The CLI, MCP and REST APIs cover every piece of your workflow, so you own the experience. Multi-tenant workspaces with optional boards per workspace, team invites, role-based permissions, and real-time collaboration for many teams. Clean Kanban boards, calendar views, a unified Inbox for mentions and updates, and a Theme picker supporting Light, Dark, AMOLED, and custom Paper theme.
## Setup options Whether you prefer a browser UI, the command line, or integrating via code, there's a path that fits your workflow.

Sign in with email on app.hypertask.ai to start collaborating immediately. Invite your team and start adding tasks, boards, and workflows.

Manage and create tasks from the terminal with the hypertask CLI. Install via your package manager, login, and start creating.

  1. Install the CLI via npm or homebrew.
  2. Run hypertask login and follow the on-screen prompts.
  3. Use commands like hypertask task create, hypertask task list, and hypertask comment add from your shell.

Connect Hypertask to your AI agents via the Model Context Protocol. The MCP server exposes tools for tasks, boards, chat, and more.

  1. Add the Hypertask MCP endpoint to your LM Studio, Claude Desktop, or another MCP-compatible client.
  2. Authenticate with a Bearer token or session cookie.
  3. Use hypertask_tasks for task creation and assignment, and hypertask_comments for replies.

Use our REST API to build integration or mobile apps. Seeds, boards, views, tasks, comments, and more are all reachable via simple HTTP requests.

  1. Get an API key from the Settings sidebar in the app.
  2. Add Authorization: Bearer <key> headers to your requests.
  3. Use endpoints like GET /boards, POST /tasks, POST /messages/chat, and more.
 ## Core concepts Here's a quick overview of the key concepts you'll use in Hypertask. | Concept | Description | |---------|-------------| | **Workspace** | The top-level container for your organization. Board owners can choose whether a board belongs to one workspace or automatically inherits from the owner. | | **Board** | A flexible surface for organizing work: Kanban columns, tables, lists, or calendars. Boards contain sections, views, and tasks. | | **Section** | A column on a Kanban board with tasks that share a common state or trigger. Sections support drag-to-reorder. | | **View** | A custom perspective on a board—filtering, sorting, grouping, or hiding tasks. Views can be pinned, hidden, or deleted as needed. | | **Task** | A unit of work with a title, description, assignee, tags, subtasks, and relations with other tasks and issues. | | **Chat** | An in-app AI assistant that understands your context—tasks, boards, messages, and more. You can create and edit saved GPTs, speed up writing, and control agents and time tracking. | | **Inbox** | A unified feed of mentions, important items, reactions, and updates across your boards. Unread items are highlighted and accessible via keyboard navigation. | | **Agents** | Autonomous AI agents that can pull context from your board, create and update tasks, respond to comments, run schedules, and interact with your workspace via tools. |
It's Email-native, but not Firebase-dependent. Hypertask uses Better Auth and your own SMTP for signing in, with Firebase kept exclusively for push notifications. You can also integrate via CLI, MCP, or REST without going through the app UI at all.
## Getting started
  1. Create an account or sign in with email/app password at app.hypertask.ai.
  2. Request a new sign-in link if your browser session expires or is shared; links are single-use, so each click gives you a fresh sign-in.
  3. Request a new verification link when creating a new account; never reuse old verification emails.
  4. Set your preferred theme using the Ctrl+K command palette or the Theme picker in Settings (Light, Dark, System, AMOLED, Paper).
  5. For email signups: You land directly on a board and receive a welcome email containing install steps for Claude Code / Cursor MCP along with a link to your board.
  6. Invite teammates to your workspace and create your first board (Kanban, Table, List, or Calendar).
  7. Start adding tasks, tagging them for organization, and assigning them.
  8. Use Ctrl+K to access the command palette for quick navigation and actions.
  9. Chat with the AI assistant to create tasks, summarize boards, or brainstorm without leaving the page.
  10. Optional: install the CLI or set up an MCP agent for programmatic control over your tasks.
 ## Keyboard shortcuts Hypertask has a rich set of keyboard shortcuts across surfaces. Press Ctrl+K to open the command palette and search for shortcuts by name.
Depending on your OS, Ctrl is Control on Windows/Linux and ⌘ on macOS.
Ctrl+K — Open command palette for shortcuts and actions. Ctrl+G — Navigate surfaces (Inbox → Boards → My Tasks → Chat), as needed. ### Live shortcuts The command palette shows all shortcuts relevant to your current context, such as boards, tasks, inbox, and chat. Hover over a shortcut to see its location (modal, board surface, or button). ### Keyboard hints in the UI The header's **Login** button shows a "Press L to log in" tooltip when you hover over it or focus it with the keyboard. This hint highlights the visual keycap style for improved discoverability and accessibility. ## Onboarding First-time users see an Onboarding Tour when they sign in. You can replay it at any time by pressing Ctrl+K, searching for "Onboarding tour", and selecting the replay option. The tour walks you through connecting AI, creating your first board, and using key features. Invited teammates see a trimmed version that skips heavy setup but still introduces essential workflows. ## Security, auth, and permissions Hypertask uses server-side authentication and ensures that other users' data never leaks into your boards or views. Here are some key principles: - Email sign-in & Better Auth: Sign in is handled server-side. Email login takes you directly to your board; magic-links and sign-out remain functional. - Firebase for push only: Firebase Auth is not used for login or signup. Firebase is strictly for FCM push notifications. - Route cleanup: Dead authentication routes that no longer exist (e.g. old signup or password reset paths) return 404, and CORS carve-outs are removed for production security. - Session integrity via signed ht_session cookies: API routes validate signed ht_session cookies alongside nookies_user, ensuring that forging cookies cannot be used for cookie spoofing. - PostHog cross-domain visitor identity: Signin and load attribution between hypertask.ai and app.hypertask.ai use signed ht_session cookies, avoiding client-side cookie dependency. - Strict account linking: Linking a Google login to an unverified local account is blocked, ensuring verified local accounts are not orphaned. - Multi-tenant isolation: By design, boards, views, and tasks belong to the user. Archive and other features show only your data unless explicitly shared. - Single-use login and verification links: When you request a new sign-in link or account verification email, the link is valid for one use only. Attempting to reuse a link shows an "invalid or expired" message and does not grant a session. - Board-level access for files: Only people who can see a ticket can download its attachments. Access is scoped to the task: observers outside the ticket cannot reach files and previews, even if they can view the board.
For finer-grained security, you can use the REST API to enforce claims, tokens, and additional checks for your integrations.
## Frequently asked questions
Is Hypertask free? The Free plan includes unlimited members and unlimited open tickets. You can own up to 3 boards. Archived boards are not counted. A paid or comped plan has no board limit. See [Billing & Seat Management](/features/billing/) for details.
Can I export my tasks? Yes. Export options include CSV, JSON, and integrations with IDEs, build tools, and CI/CD pipelines using the CLI and REST API.
Is there a mobile app? Yes. Android has an official app, and iPhone and other phones install the web app with Add to Home Screen. See [Mobile and desktop apps](/getting-started/apps/).
Is there a desktop app for Windows or Mac? Use the web app in a browser, or install it as an app. There is no signed desktop download. See [Mobile and desktop apps](/getting-started/apps/).

title: Claude Haiku 5.5 replaces Haiku 4.5
description: Claude Haiku 5.5 has been released as the default AI model, offering consistent behavior across all AI features.
---

Claude Haiku 5.5 has been released as the new default AI model for everyone, replacing Haiku 4.5. The change brings consistent model behavior across all AI surfaces including AI Task Writer, Agent Chat, and code-generation workflows.

**Model choice and behavior:**
- Haiku 5.5 now serves as the default model for all new AI conversations
- The replacement reduces confusion around having multiple Haiku versions live simultaneously
- Model quality reflects real-world usage patterns and usage-based cost

**Real-world cost:**
In live measurements on the QA Sandbox board, Claude Haiku 5.5 costs approximately 1.7x more per request than GPT 6 Luna. This difference stems from longer answer lengths rather than per-token pricing parity:

```
AI chat, 10 prompts each on the same board:
- Haiku 5.5: 1.70x cost of GPT 6 Luna per request
- All models use identical per-token pricing
```

The model is fully operational on all supported environments including Free and paid subscription tiers.

When Haiku 5.5 is selected (or left as default), it behaves equivalently to GPT 6 Luna in all supported AI workflows, ensuring predictable outputs regardless of model provider.

title: Appearance & AI Models
description: Customize themes, icons, fonts, and select AI models for Hypertask.
---


## Appearance Settings

### Light and dark themes

Hypertask supports both light and dark themes, controlled from your profile or the Command Center.

- **Dark theme** â\x80\x94 reduces eye strain when working in low-light environments and is ideal for long coding sessions.
- **Light theme** â\x80\x94 provides high contrast for collaborative reviews and when sharing your screen.

You can toggle themes instantly from the settings menu. Preferences are saved per-user.

In AMOLED, floating AI chat has a thin outline and compact corners so it stays distinct from the black page, on desktop and phone. Other themes keep their existing appearance.

### Graphite 2

Choose **Graphite 2** in **Settings → Appearance**. Or open **Ctrl+K**, search **Graphite 2**, and press **Enter**.

Graphite 2 uses a quiet dark-grey palette, IBM Plex Sans, and Iconoir sidebar icons. Task titles use a lighter weight, while tags stay unfilled. Your choice survives a reload. **Dark · Graphite** and the other themes keep their existing appearance.

## Keyboard shortcuts

From the Command Center, use **Ctrl+K** to open the global command palette. While focusing on a task detail, you can also use:

- **Ctrl+O** â\x80\x94 Open links from the latest reply in a new tab (Agent Chat and board comments).
- **Alt+Left/Right** â\x80\x94 Navigate through tasks or agents in increasing or decreasing order.

These shortcuts are available across boards, chat panels, and the Agents overview.

<Aside type="tip">

Some shortcuts are also active in the main command palette when a compatible view is loaded.

</Aside>

## Text editor preferences

### Comments and descriptions

When composing comments or editing task descriptions, you can:

- Dictate **Ctrl+K**, **Ctrl+Space** (on supported browsers): Start voice dictation from the text field.
- Save **Ctrl+Enter**: Send the comment; the task may stay or advance depending on context.
- Open links **Ctrl+O**: When a reply includes a clickable link, open it in a new tab.

The comment composer is pinned to the bottom of task detail panels, keeping it accessible while you read and compose.

## AI models

### Model selection

Hypertask supports multiple AI providers and models. During configuration, agents operate with provider-specific model names. Agent Chat respects the engine configured on an agent:

- **Claude-based agents** use Claude models (for example, claude-sonnet-5).
- **Codex-based agents** use Codex models (for example, gpt-5.6-luna).

The chat lane configuration must align with the agent's engine.

<Aside type="note">

You do not need OpenRouter-specific keys in Hypertask; the runtime handles exchange of credentials and model mapping. If you plan to use OpenRouter lanes beyond the default provider, include OPENROUTER_GLM_API_KEY for squad-based workflows.

</Aside>

**Claude Haiku 5.5** is now Hypertask's default AI model for everyone, replacing Haiku 4.5. The new default is available across all plans, offering consistent model behavior for all users. When Haiku 5.5 is selected, it behaves equivalently to GPT 6 Luna in all supported surfaces including AI Task Writer, Agent Chat, and code-generation workflows.

Model quality now reflects real-world usage: Claude Haiku 5.5 cost per request is approximately 1.7× higher than GPT 6 Luna due to longer answer lengths, though the per-token price is identical. The model is fully operational on all supported environments, including Free and paid subscriptions.

<Aside type="tip">

Once the model is selected in your profile, the choice applies globally to any AI feature you use, keeping agent behavior and output style consistent across tasks, boards, and workspace contexts.

</Aside>

### Quiet mode

Quiet mode controls how agent activity appears in run activities and thread comments. It applies to agents in active runs:

- **Run activity** â\x80\x94 by default, agents write detailed progress chatter to the run activity tab. Quiet mode suppresses most run activity logs.
- **Thread comments** â\x80\x94 quiet mode disables comment generation. Comments are only posted for specific actions:
  - Question
  - Decision
  - Handoff
  - Done

When running in quiet mode, agents remain fully engaged, but their directional footprint in the task history is streamlined. To enable quiet mode, use the `quiet-run-activity` token or configure it via board-level agent settings.

<Aside type="tip">

Quiet mode is useful for workflow histories where you want to review agent behavior via structured run logs, but keep thread conversations focused on human decisions and actions.

</Aside>

## Icons, fonts, and visual tokens

### Sidebar icons

Icon visual standards are managed in the Typography & Sidebar Visuals page. Controlled strokes and consistent spacing ensure icons are legible across light and dark modes.

### Font scale

Typography uses a defined type scale for headlines, descriptions, and UI labels. Choose consistent weights and sizes from the standard set to maintain visual hierarchy.

### Component reuse checklist

When adding UI controls to the app, define the existing component being reused or provide a specific reason. This checklist applies to all UI pull requests and is enforced via the canonical guide and required gate. Each new control must be mapped to an underlying component or documented with a no-reuse justification.

<Aside type="note">

Requests that reference or implement reusable components should include a mapping for each control added. Reviewers use the checklist to verify reusability claims and avoid unnecessary component proliferation.

</Aside>

title: Profile & Settings
description: Manage your identity, appearance, and preferences in Hypertask.
---


Your Profile page in Hypertask is split into three dedicated sections: **General**, **Appearance**, and **Task page**. Each has its own navigation point and can be accessed directly from anywhere in the app via `Ctrl+K`.

---

## General

The **General** tab contains your identity settings:

- **Avatar** — Upload or change your profile picture.
- **Display name** — The name shown to others in tasks, comments, and activity feeds.
- **Email** — Your primary email address; used for notifications and logins.
- **Bio** (optional) — A short description shown in your profile card.

Use these fields to manage how you appear across the platform.

## Session settings

Hypertask uses Better Auth server-side authentication with configurable login session duration:

- **Session length** — Choose between 7 days and 30 days when signing in. This controls how long your session stays active before requiring re-authentication.
- **Persistent sign-in links** — Access a persistent sign-in link that doesn't expire until used.
- **Clean sign-out** — All flows support immediate session invalidation and cookie clearing.

## Privacy & cookies

Hypertask respects your right to control how your data is collected. By default, tracking is disabled until you make an explicit choice:

- **No tracking until consent** — Tracking cookies and IP lookups are not stored or performed until you select an option.
- **Consent banner** — Every visitor sees a cookie banner on login, signup, and when you open a signed-in board.
- **Shared consent choice** — Your tracking preferences on hypertask.ai are shared across all Hypertask products and tracked behavior follows your choice.

This ensures your data is not collected without your knowledge or agreement.

---

## Appearance

The **Appearance** tab controls the visual look of your interface:

- **Theme** — Choose between Light, Dark, or System theme (automatically follows your OS preference).
- **Font size** — Adjust text size across the app for better readability.
- **Reduced motion** — Reduce animations for a calmer environment.

## Task page

The **Task page** tab configures behavior specific to how tasks display:

- **Show task scroll** (on/off) — When enabled, Hypertask automatically scrolls to the full task description and details when opening a task.
- **Subtask depth** — Control how many levels of subtasks are visible by default.
- **Expand inline details** — Show fields like due date, assignee, and labels inline on the task card.

These settings apply to the task detail view and the task editor across all boards.

## AI settings

The **AI Settings** tab in the Task page section allows you to configure how the AI assistant behaves across your tasks and comments:

- **Custom instructions** — Provide board-level instructions that the AI follows when helping with tasks on that board. Enter your instructions directly into the text box, which fills the page to give you maximum writing space and easy visibility of full context.

These instructions are applied automatically when the AI drafts responses, edits descriptions, or proposes next steps in chat or comments.

## Ask the AI to change a setting

On any Settings page you can ask the AI chat, in plain words, for a change on that page:

- Say what you want: "switch me to the dark theme", "turn off email notifications for comments", or "make Anna an admin on this board".
- The reply carries one **Setting change** card showing the setting, its current value and the new value. Nothing changes until you press **Apply**; press **Cancel** and nothing happens.
- Once a change lands, the card offers **Undo**, which puts the previous value back.
- The card also shows **Open setting**, so you can go to the control yourself.

The AI uses your own rights, exactly as if you clicked. A board member cannot change what only the board owner may change, and access and people changes always go through the same card. If a change is not something it can make, it tells you where the setting lives and opens that page.

## User profile caching

On authenticated startup, Hypertask reuses a fresh account-scoped user profile cached at the app shell layer. The cached profile remains valid for about 5 minutes, reducing repeated `/api/users/getById` refetches and improving cold start performance. The cache is automatically invalidated and refreshed as needed.

## Preferences via signed login

Preferences now load and save correctly with a signed login alone, without requiring the older profile cookie. As long as your session is signed in, the Preferences page can read and write settings such as Play GIFs, text size, and theme, and changes persist across reloads.

```bash
# Signed in with your session only
# Navigate to Settings → Task page
# Toggle Play GIFs or adjust a setting
# The change is saved immediately and survives navigation
```

This simplifies session handling so a single authentication flow serves all content and settings across the app.

## Management keys

Management keys let API, CLI, MCP, and AI chat clients manage agents and credentials. Create them under **Settings → Connect → Management keys**, next to MCP, CLI, and REST API.

<Steps>

1. Open [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai) and sign in.
2. Open **Settings**, then **Connect**, then **Management keys**.
3. Enter a name, choose a scope, and choose an expiry.
4. Choose **Create key**. Copy the key immediately. It is shown once.

</Steps>

**Scope** is **Management**, **Usage**, or **Full access**. Full access stays on the whole account. Usage reads team AI usage and spend. Management manages agents and keys.

**Expiry** is **Never**, **30 days**, **90 days**, or **365 days**. A new management key starts on **Never**. The list shows **Expires** and a date, or **Never**.

When team-scoped keys are available, Management and Usage can be limited to one team. Full access cannot. A team key stops working if you lose access to that team.

REST API keys are on the same **Connect** screen, under **Developer access**. They use the same four expiry choices, and a new REST API key starts on **90 days**.

If a client is refused after a key's date, see [MCP troubleshooting](/mcp/troubleshooting/).

## Common Actions

### Change your avatar or name

1. Open your Profile page in the app.
2. Switch to the **General** tab.
3. Upload a new image or edit your name under the Avatar or Display name fields.
4. Click **Save** to apply changes.

See [Keyboard Shortcuts](/features/keyboard-shortcuts/) for cmd-k access to Profile and General.

## Keyboard Shortcuts

For quick navigation within Profile:

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| `Ctrl+K` then type "Profile" | Open the full Profile page |
| `Ctrl+K` then type "General" | Jump to General tab |
| `Ctrl+K` then type "Appearance" | Jump to Appearance tab |
| `Ctrl+K` then type "Task" | Jump to Task page tab |

--- title: Agent webhooks description: Understand what wakes an agent, what Hypertask sends, how to verify it, and how to work without a public URL. --- A webhook is an instant notification from Hypertask to your agent. When a selected event happens, Hypertask sends a signed HTTPS request to one receiver you control. Polling still works without a webhook, but the agent learns about changes on its next check instead of immediately. ## Get your first verified delivery 1. In Hypertask, press **Ctrl+K**, open **Manage agents**, then select the plug icon beside your agent. 2. Under **Wake this agent without polling**, enter your public HTTPS receiver. Optionally limit delivery to one board or a subset of events. 3. Select **Save webhook** and store the signing secret. Hypertask shows it once. 4. Select **Send test**. Your receiver gets a real signed `webhook.test` delivery through the same queue and retry path as production events. 5. Confirm a 2xx result under **Recent deliveries**. Failed deliveries show their status and can be replayed.
Store the `whsec_…` signing secret in your secret manager. Hypertask masks it after creation. Rotate it if it is lost or exposed.
## Subscribe from an agent An agent bearer token manages its own endpoint with `self`. A human account token can replace `self` with an owned agent UUID. ```bash # Configure all addressed events hypertask webhook configure \ --url https://agent.example.com/hypertask \ --event comment.mention \ --event task.assigned \ --event task.unassigned \ --event comment.created \ --event task.updated \ --event task.created # Prove the receiver, signature, queue, and response path hypertask webhook test # Inspect delivery status hypertask webhook get ``` Use `--agent AGENT_UUID` when running with a human account token. Other commands are `replay DELIVERY_ID`, `rotate-secret`, and `delete`. Call `hypertask_webhooks` (`action: "configure"`): ```json { "action": "configure", "input": { "agent_id": "self", "url": "https://agent.example.com/hypertask", "events": ["comment.mention", "task.assigned", "task.unassigned", "comment.created", "task.updated", "task.created"] } } ``` Actions are `get`, `configure`, `test`, `replay`, `rotate`, and `delete`. `replay` also requires `delivery_id`. In private AI Chat, ask in plain language: > Configure the webhook for my Release Agent at https://agent.example.com/hypertask, then send a test. Secret-bearing and write actions require confirmation before they run. Hypertask shows a preview first; approve it in your next message. In a HyperAI ticket comment, `get`, `test`, `replay`, and `delete` are available with the same confirmation policy. Configure or rotate in private AI Chat, CLI, MCP, or agent settings because HyperAI never writes signing secrets into persistent ticket comments. ```bash curl -X POST https://app.hypertask.ai/api/mcp/webhooks \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENT_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "action": "configure", "agent_id": "self", "url": "https://agent.example.com/hypertask", "events": ["comment.mention", "task.assigned", "task.unassigned", "comment.created", "task.updated", "task.created"] }' ``` The response contains `secret` once. Read configuration and recent attempts with: ```bash curl "https://app.hypertask.ai/api/mcp/webhooks?agent_id=self" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENT_TOKEN" ``` ## Board-level webhooks Each managed agent has one webhook subscription. Leave **Board scope** empty to receive selected events from every board the agent belongs to, or choose one board to narrow delivery. Hypertask stops delivery if the agent loses that board membership or is revoked. Only the agent owner can view, configure, test, replay, rotate, or delete its webhook. Agent credentials may manage their own webhook with `agent_id: "self"`; a human credential must name an agent it owns. ## Verify the signature Hypertask signs the exact raw request bytes. Verify them before parsing JSON; parsing and reserializing can change the signed content. | Header | Meaning | |---|---| | `X-Hypertask-Event` | Event name, including `webhook.test` | | `X-Hypertask-Timestamp` | Unix time used in the signature | | `X-Hypertask-Delivery` | Stable ID used to deduplicate automatic retries | | `X-Hypertask-Signature` | `sha256=` followed by the lowercase HMAC hex digest | ```text signed content = X-Hypertask-Timestamp + "." + raw request bytes signature = "sha256=" + HMAC-SHA256(signing secret, signed content) ``` Use a constant-time comparison and reject timestamps outside your replay window. The examples use five minutes. ```js const app = express(); const secret = process.env.HYPERTASK_WEBHOOK_SECRET; app.post("/hypertask", express.raw({ type: "application/json" }), (req, res) => { const rawBody = req.body; const timestamp = req.header("x-hypertask-timestamp") ?? ""; const received = req.header("x-hypertask-signature") ?? ""; const timestampSeconds = Number(timestamp); if (!secret || !Buffer.isBuffer(rawBody) || !Number.isFinite(timestampSeconds) || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - timestampSeconds) > 300) { return res.sendStatus(401); } const digest = createHmac("sha256", secret) .update(`${timestamp}.`) .update(rawBody) .digest("hex"); const expected = `sha256=${digest}`; const left = Buffer.from(received, "utf8"); const right = Buffer.from(expected, "utf8"); if (left.length !== right.length || !timingSafeEqual(left, right)) { return res.sendStatus(401); } const deliveryId = req.header("x-hypertask-delivery"); const payload = JSON.parse(rawBody.toString("utf8")); res.sendStatus(202); // Store deliveryId before queueing work so retries do not run twice. }); ``` ```python from flask import Flask, request app = Flask(__name__) secret = os.environ["HYPERTASK_WEBHOOK_SECRET"].encode() @app.post("/hypertask") def handle_webhook(): raw_body = request.get_data(cache=True) timestamp = request.headers.get("X-Hypertask-Timestamp", "") received = request.headers.get("X-Hypertask-Signature", "") try: if abs(time.time() - int(timestamp)) > 300: return "stale timestamp", 401 except ValueError: return "invalid timestamp", 401 signed = timestamp.encode() + b"." + raw_body expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret, signed, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest() if not hmac.compare_digest(received, expected): return "invalid signature", 401 delivery_id = request.headers.get("X-Hypertask-Delivery") payload = json.loads(raw_body) # queueAgentWork(delivery_id, payload) return "", 202 ``` ## Events and payloads | Event | When it fires | Event-only fields | |---|---|---| | `comment.mention` | A comment mentions this exact agent | `commentId`, `commentHtml` | | `task.assigned` | This agent becomes a task assignee | Common task fields only | | `task.unassigned` | This agent is removed from a task | Common task fields only | | `comment.created` | Any comment is added to a task assigned to this agent | `commentId`, `commentHtml` | | `task.updated` | A task in scope changes section, status, or labels | `changes`, optional `labelsRedacted` | | `task.created` | Task creation and automatic column assignment finish in scope | `assignees`, `labels`, optional `labelsRedacted` | | `webhook.test` | The owner selects **Send test** or requests a test | `test: true`, `message`; no task fields | Task event payloads include `event`, `deliveryId`, `occurredAt`, `agentId`, `projectId`, `taskId`, nullable `ticketNumber`, `taskTitle`, and `actor`. Event-only fields appear as shown above. A test payload has the common delivery fields but no task or actor. ```json { "event": "comment.mention", "deliveryId": "53d179e1-84b8-48a3-807a-cf8e5b88930b", "occurredAt": "2026-08-13T10:15:00.000Z", "agentId": "f95165ad-36b3-4d87-af70-547df78e17c1", "projectId": 15, "taskId": 27397, "taskTitle": "Outbound webhooks for agent mentions and assignments", "commentId": 182293, "commentHtml": "

@Release Agent please review

", "actor": { "userId": 6, "agentId": null, "displayName": "Valentin Yeo" } } ``` ## Test and replay **Send test** creates a real `webhook.test` delivery for the active subscription. It uses the same signed request, queue, retry schedule, and recent-delivery list as production events, without requiring a task change. **Replay** is available only to the agent owner and only for a delivery from that agent's current subscription. It copies the stored event payload into a new delivery with a new delivery ID, transport timestamp, and signature. The receiver must treat replay as a possible duplicate of the original work. ## Delivery behavior - Hypertask sends the first `POST` immediately with `Content-Type: application/json`. - Return any 2xx response within **5 seconds**. Queue longer work after responding. - A failed `chat.message` attempt remains available to agent polling while its normal webhook retries continue. If polling claims the message first, Hypertask cancels the outstanding webhook retry so the agent cannot process it twice. Deleting the webhook also releases chat messages that have not been acknowledged. - Events retry after a timeout, network failure, unsafe address, redirect, or any other non-2xx response. Delays after the first, second, and third failed attempts are approximately **30 seconds, 5 minutes, and 30 minutes**. Delivery stops after four total attempts. - Automatic retries keep the exact body and delivery ID. Each attempt gets a fresh timestamp and signature. Store `X-Hypertask-Delivery` before starting work so a retry cannot run the same action twice. - Recent delivered, failed, and cancelled outcomes remain visible for 30 days. ## No public HTTPS URL A webhook cannot point to `localhost` or a private network address. You can expose only your receiver through a temporary tunnel, or skip the webhook and poll. ### Use a temporary Cloudflare Tunnel 1. Start your receiver locally, for example at `http://localhost:3000/hypertask`. 2. Run `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:3000`. 3. Copy the generated `https://…trycloudflare.com` address, add `/hypertask`, and save it as the webhook endpoint. 4. Select **Send test**, then confirm a 2xx result under **Recent deliveries**.
Expose only the webhook route. Do not run a debug server or expose admin routes. Keep the signing secret in an environment variable, do not print secrets or full production payloads, and stop the tunnel when testing ends. Quick Tunnel addresses change when restarted, so update the saved endpoint before testing again.
### Poll instead A webhook is optional. `hypertask agent poll` reads unseen comments that mention the active agent. A persistent worker can also reconcile assignments and its configured board queue through normal authenticated reads, which catches a missed webhook. ```bash hypertask agent poll \ --project "$PROJECT_ID" \ --agent-id "$AGENT_ID" \ --agent-name "$AGENT_NAME" ``` Polling cadence belongs to the worker deployment, not the Hypertask API. Set an explicit active and idle interval in the worker profile. For example, `pollFastSeconds: 60` checks every minute while work is active and `pollSlowSeconds: 3600` checks hourly while idle. A webhook remains the instant path; reconciliation is the slower safety net. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Check | |---|---| | No secret appears | Secrets are shown only after first configuration or rotation. Rotate if the original was not stored. | | Test stays pending | Confirm the endpoint is public HTTPS and wait for queue delivery. If it is local, start the tunnel and save its current address. | | `401` from your receiver | Verify the raw bytes before parsing and include `timestamp + "."` before the body. | | Repeated work | Deduplicate with `X-Hypertask-Delivery`; automatic retries are intentionally at least once. | | `4xx` while configuring | The agent must belong to the selected board, and the URL cannot resolve to a private or reserved address. | | No production events | Confirm **Delivery enabled**, selected event names, board scope, and current agent board membership. |

title: Switching from Trello, Jira, or Asana
description: Switching from Trello, Jira, Asana, or Linear. Hypertask has no task import. Create tasks with an agent over MCP or the CLI.
---

Switching from Trello, Jira, or Asana usually starts with two questions: whether existing tasks can move over, and how Hypertask differs from Linear or Jira.

## Importing tasks

Hypertask has no task import. There is no one-click import from Trello, Jira, Asana, or Linear. The import routes in the product import [AI skills](/features/skills/), not tasks.

Export a CSV from the old tool. Connect an agent over [MCP](/mcp/overview/) or the [CLI](/cli/reference/), and ask it to create the tasks from that file.

- CLI: [`hypertask task create`](/cli/commands/#hypertask-task-create) creates one task. It needs a project id and a title.
- MCP: [`hypertask_tasks`](/api/tools-reference/#hypertask_tasks) with action `create` creates one task the same way.

[Agent workflows](/mcp/workflows/) describe how an agent lists board work and creates tasks.

## How Hypertask differs

- **Keyboard-first UI.** The [search screen](/features/search-screen/) is a keyboard-first way to find tasks, and the app publishes its [keyboard shortcuts](/features/keyboard-shortcuts/).
- **AI agents.** Agents [pick up board work](/mcp/workflows/) over MCP and the CLI.
- **BYOK plan.** [Bring Your Own Key](/features/byok/) uses your own model keys. [Included AI](/features/ai-features/#included-ai-allowance) describes the Free, Pro, and BYOK allowances.

---
title: Integrations
description: What Hypertask connects to today, including Cursor and Codex, and what is not available yet.
---

Hypertask works with Cursor and Codex. Both connect through MCP, the same way as any other MCP client.

## Works today

These are in **Settings**, then **Connect**:

- **[MCP](/mcp/overview/).** Works with any MCP client, such as Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.
- **[CLI](/cli/reference/).** The `hypertask` command.
- **[REST API](/api/rest-api/).**
- **[Webhooks](/mcp/agent-webhooks/).** Signed requests to a URL you control.

**Figma** is under **Settings**, then **Profile**, then **Accounts**. Connect a Figma account there. Hypertask uses that connection when a task includes a Figma link.

**ChatGPT** uses an OpenAPI action. The steps are on [MCP Integration](/mcp/overview/#client-configuration), under the ChatGPT tab.

## Not available yet

- **Slack app.** Not available yet.
- **GitHub per board.** Connecting GitHub to a board is not available yet.
- **Google Calendar sync.** Not available yet. Due dates still appear on the Hypertask [calendar](/features/calendar/).
- **Other importers.** There is no Jira, Trello, or Asana sync, and no other native importer.

## Context and projects

### `hypertask_projects`

Does: List accessible boards, read their column manifests and playbooks, create or rename boards, and manage board settings and members.
Use when: Use to discover project_id or section_id before ticket changes, or to build a board from a brief using the create action.
Do not use when: Do not use to move individual tickets or change a column; use hypertask_tasks or hypertask_sections instead.
Parameters and caveats: action selects an operation; input contains only that operation’s documented fields. response_format defaults to concise for reads; detailed retains full fields. limit defaults to 20 (maximum 50) and offset defaults to 0 for bounded read results; use returned pagination or narrower filters. A project is a board and a section is a column; manifest returns ordered columns and their semantic roles. Creating a board accepts nested tasks and section names, and archive changes visibility without deleting it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `action` | `list` \| `manifest` \| `playbook` \| `create` \| `rename` \| `members` \| `archive` \| `invite_member` \| `get_playbook` \| `set_playbook` \| `get_instructions` \| `set_instructions` \| `hygiene` \| `github_repos` \| `set_github_repos` | Yes | Operation to perform on this resource. |
| `input` | object \| object \| object \| object \| object \| object \| object \| object \| object \| object \| object \| object \| object \| object \| object | No | Action-specific fields documented in the corresponding input schema. Fields depend on action; use the variant whose title is the action. |
| `limit` | integer | No | Maximum rows per read collection; default 20, maximum 50. Defaults to `20`. |
| `offset` | integer | No | Rows to skip for paginated or locally bounded reads; default 0. Prefer an input cursor when supplied. Defaults to `0`. |
| `page` | integer | No | 1-based page number; page 1 is the first page. An offset that equals the page start is accepted; any other offset is refused. |
| `response_format` | `concise` \| `detailed` | No | Concise summarizes reads; detailed includes full fields. Writes always retain their receipts. Defaults to `concise`. |

### `hypertask_user_context`

Does: Orient to the authenticated user, their accessible boards and account connections, list every enabled feature-kind flag and core product destinations with verified URLs where known, or update their own profile.

##### Hello guided start

Call `hypertask_user_context` with `action: "hello"` for a guided start in MCP v2 (consolidated tools, on for Everyone). The legacy catalog exposes `hypertask_hello`. `GET https://mcp.hypertask.ai/api/mcp/hello` returns the same guide.

| Field | What it contains |
|-------|------------------|
| `agent` | The agent's `id` and `displayName`. It is `null` for a personal user token. |
| `startBoard` | The newest board across all boards the token can see, with `id`, `title`, and `boardUrl`. A missing title falls back to the short name. It is `null` when no board is available. |
| `nextSteps` | Three suggested steps for write agents, or two for read-only agents (no create step). No board means an empty list. Each has `step`, a CLI `command`, an MCP `tool`, and MCP `arguments`. |

Each step uses the tool name and argument shape advertised by `tools/list` for the same credential. For the fictional board Product Launch (`9142`), the default consolidated steps for a write agent are:

| Step | CLI command | MCP tool | MCP arguments |
|------|-------------|----------|---------------|
| See the board | `hypertask task list --project 9142` | `hypertask_tasks` | `{"action":"list","input":{"project_id":9142}}` |
| Create a first task | `hypertask task create --project 9142 --title "My first task"` | `hypertask_tasks` | `{"action":"create","input":{"project_id":9142,"title":"My first task"}}` |
| Read the board rules | `hypertask project playbook 9142` | `hypertask_projects` | `{"action":"playbook","input":{"project_id":9142}}` |

The legacy catalog instead uses `hypertask_list_tasks`, `hypertask_create_task`, and `hypertask_get_board_playbook`, with arguments at the top level (no `action` or `input` wrapper). Read-only agents receive only the list and playbook steps.

The tool description asks MCP clients to say who they are signed in as and offer these steps. For a write agent, for example: "Signed in as Claude Code (agent of Maria Lopez). Your board is Product Launch. Would you like to see the board, create a first task, or read the board rules?"

## Comments

### `hypertask_comments`

Does: List, add, edit, delete, pin or star ticket comments. Untyped agent notes stay hidden, including replies and mentions. Files require kind. Use question for decisions, qa for verdicts, or done for summaries. People comments use short plain sentences; technical details and status belong in the agent log. A hidden log post answers 202, not 201.
Use when: Use to discuss a ticket or inspect its conversation; list with include_activity also retrieves work history, and pin keeps one answer at the top. For a person to decide, add a ticket comment with a line starting Question: and @mention that person using a real mention, not just their name. The mention notification appears in their Inbox; when Decisions is enabled for them and the notification is visible, the unanswered ticket appears in Inbox, split Decisions: https://app.hypertask.ai/inbox?split=Decisions. A later non-agent comment by that person on the ticket removes it from Decisions. Ordinary mentions are not Decisions. Structured decision records are separate; creating one alone does not create this Question: + @mention workflow. Use a comment, not a page, to request a decision.
Do not use when: Do not use for ticket descriptions or unpublished drafts; use hypertask_tasks or hypertask_drafts instead.

title: Human comments notify assigned agents
description: A person's comment on a ticket now notifies assigned and following agents in their inbox and through webhooks. Agents no longer see their own comments in these feeds, keeping notifications relevant and accurate.
---

A person's plain comment on a ticket now reliably notifies all assigned and following agents in their in-app inbox and through your configured webhook integrations. This change closes the gap between human and agent workflows, ensuring team members are immediately aware of updates that affect them without cluttering notifications with their own reflections.

For a comment author, the experience remains the same: type your message as you normally would on a ticket. The system no longer echoes back the author as a recipient, so your own comment won't trigger an extra notification for you.

For agents and any other interested listeners, the ticket's comment appears at the top of their inbox as a new item, sorted by recent updates. The change applies across desktop and mobile, and works with the existing webhook pipeline-if you've connected Slack, email, or another tool via webhooks, those integrations receive the notification alongside the in-app inbox.

What changed
- Added post-comment routing logic for inbox notification targets
- Updated webhook payload structure to include comment author and assignment context
- Guard against self-notification by marking comment author as excluded from recipient lists

How it affects you
- Assigned agents and anyone following a ticket now see every human comment arrive instantly
- You can rely on the inbox and webhooks as a single source of truth for task-related updates
- No manual @mentions are required for this behavior to take effect; it applies to all plain comments

The inbox is already the place where team members process notifications efficiently, so this change strengthens its role as the central hub for task discussions. Webhook recipients maintain their existing integration logic while now receiving consistent, complete notification data.

title: Agents Dashboard
description: View all your agents from a central dashboard, with detail pages for each agent, board-scoped view, and status toggles at a glance.

# Agents Dashboard

The **Agents Dashboard** gives you a central view of your agents, including summary statistics, per-agent details, and board-scoped dashboards.

## Access the Agents Dashboard

- **URL**: `https://app.hypertask.ai/agents`
- From any page, use `Cmd+K` (Mac), `Ctrl+K` (Windows/Linux) and search for **"Go to Agents"**.

## Agent list by status

The overview page (`/agents`) groups your agents into three top-level sections:

- **Running** — agents currently active and executing tasks.
- **Quiet** — agents not currently running, but ready to start.
- **Off** — agents paused or stopped.

Each group displays agent cards showing key information.

## Agent cards

Each agent card shows:

- **Agent name** — the agent identifier.
- **Status** — Running, Quiet, or Off.
- **On/Off toggle** — pause or resume the agent.
- **Heartbeat line** for the merge/unblock timer.
- **Avatar** — a generated robot icon for each agent.

### Heartbeat line

The heartbeat line visualizes the agent's 10-minute merge/unblock check:

- **Green dot, short bar** — timer ran within the last 15 minutes.
- **Amber dot, medium bar** — timer ran between 15–30 minutes ago.
- **Red dot, no bar** — timer missed its 10-minute window or no data available.

### Card outlines

A red outline signals a **blocked** agent — no one is actively working on it. This helps you spot bottlenecks at a glance.

### Blocked-summary widget

A blocked-summary widget shows the number of agents currently blocked, helping you prioritize follow-up work.

## Board-scoped agent pages

Each board has its own dedicated agent page showing the agents configured for that board:

- **URL format**: `https://app.hypertask.ai/agents/<board-number>`
- Example: Board 5500 is available at `https://app.hypertask.ai/agents/5500`.

The board page includes:

- Board-specific agent list.
- Toolkit bug totals, including AGTE tickets tagged as bug.
- Configuration source: board, repository, branch, and agent list read from a shared setup.
- Main merge counts or reference links for the board.

Use board pages to inspect board-level agent health and bug tracking per board.

## Per-agent availability

All agents show generated robot avatars from their detail pages and the dashboard. This provides visual recognition without relying on initials or external icons.

### Agent examples

| Agent | Status |
|---|---|
| Preview Bot | Running |
| QA Agent | Quiet |
| Scheduler | Off |

## Performance and reliability

Use the agents page to:

- Spot which agents are actively working.
- Pause or resume agents consuming resources.
- Monitor agent distribution across workflows.
- Identify blocked agents via red outlines and the blocked-summary widget.

## MCP client evaluation frame

When the MCP client eval is enabled, the agents page displays a table of 20 real Hypertask tasks run through the MCP server and CLI. Each row shows pass/fail, token in/out, wall time, and tool call count. This helps you compare MCP to the CLI and catch regressions.

## Working with pages and task detail pages

Agents can reference task detail pages (e.g., `/detail/project-15/<ticket>`) via the production verifier, enabling them to verify lifecycles and create links as part of workflows.

## Troubleshooting

<Aside type="note">

If you don't see an agent in the dashboard, check that:

1. The agent is connected to an active board.
2. The agent schedule has necessary permissions.
3. The agent is associated with your team or scope.

See [AI Agents](/features/agents/) and [Scheduling Agents](/mcp/scheduling/) for setup details.

</Aside>

Owner+QA preview. --- # Search Screen The search screen provides a focused, keyboard-first way to find tasks across your board. It adopts a Superhuman-inspired design: a single aligned list of recent searches and tips, grey value completions (operator and values), and keyboard-driven workflows while deferring results until selection or Enter. ## Enhanced search preview: Owner+QA only This enhanced search screen is a strict preview available to the Owner and QA roles. It is not a general release and does not require any minimum activity threshold. If you see the normal search UI, ensure you are on a checked board and the search preview flag is enabled for your account or team. ## Layout and structure Top-level search shows a consistent list: - **Recent searches**: A single list of your most recent searches. - **Tips**: Helpful hints below recent searches (operator shortcuts, example queries). - **AI panel**: Fixed on the right side, leaving the core search interface on the left. No floating boxes. The suggestions list is full-width and aligned with the search box on desktop and mobile. - **Mobile board tabs**: Under the search box, board tabs sit clearly above the bottom navigation, tapable with ample spacing and swipe-friendly when many boards exist. - **Desktop**: Board tabs follow the same layout, for the same filter behavior across devices. ## Empty and loaded states - **Empty search**: Recent searches (or none, if you have none) appear once, then tips below them. The AI panel stays fixed on the right side; the left side is free for search only. - **Loaded search**: After selecting a suggestion or pressing Enter, aligned results appear under the suggestions list. Results do not start loading until you accept a suggestion or press Enter. ## Grey inline value completion As you type, the inline suggestions box shows: - **Top suggestion**: Completed in grey inside the list. Accept with Tab. - **Operators**: Hinted inline (e.g., el: hints label:). - **Values**: Top value preview in grey (e.g., from:mal shows Malcolm Stern). This applies to common value types: people (names + emails), labels, boards. Results do not trigger while you type; they load only after you pick a suggestion or press Enter. **Example**: Type from:val; the top suggestion Valentin Yeo appears in grey; select it with Tab to trigger a board fetch and show results. ## Tips panel Under recent searches, tips explain operators the first time you open search: - Ctrl+K / Cmd+K — open command palette. - from:, assignee:, in:, label:, is:, dates:, has:, priority: — field modifiers. - "quoted phrase" — exact phrase match. - -word — exclude tasks with a word or phrase. - Press Tab on an inline value to accept it; choose Ask AI, operators, people, labels, or boards. ## Keyboard shortcuts (search UI) - Ctrl+K / Cmd+K — open command palette. - Enter — apply selected suggestion and load results. - Tab — accept and grey the top inline suggestion and load results. - Shift+Tab — previous suggestion. - Esc — clear or dismiss panels. ## Sample workflows 1. Click the search box or press /. Empty state: recent searches and tips appear. 2. Type a partial term or operator (e.g., from:mal). Inline completion shows the top value in grey. Results do not load yet. 3. Select a suggestion with Tab (or hover & click). Results load under the suggestions list. 4. Press Esc to clear and return to the recents/tips layout; results are removed. ## Status notes - This new search screen replaces the live results from the previous iconic live-results approach and works behind the existing search flags. - Verified live for Owner and QA; full release plan to widen the flag is out of scope for this documentation.

On mobile devices, the comment composer keeps dictation as the primary input method with simplified controls:

| Select project from filters | <kbd>Space</kbd> | <kbd>Space</kbd> |
| Filter tasks | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>F</kbd> | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>F</kbd> |

## Unarchive View (g -> e)

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Unarchive task | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>E</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>E</kbd> |
| Delete task | <kbd>#</kbd> | <kbd>#</kbd> |

## Command Palette

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Open command palette | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> |
| Search commands | Type to filter | Type to filter |
| Execute command | <kbd>Enter</kbd> | <kbd>Enter</kbd> |
| Navigate through filtered commands | <kbd>Arrow keys</kbd> | <kbd>Arrow keys</kbd> |

<Aside type="tip">
The Command Palette lists board and section actions, including "Hide column", "Show columns", "Archive board", "Delete board", and more. Use <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> and type keywords like "hide", "show", "archive", "delete" to quickly access relevant actions.
</Aside>

### Board settings from Ctrl+K
When you search for **"Board settings"** in the Command Palette using <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd>, the board picker now preselects the board you came from. This works whether you're on a ticket page, board page, or another view - even if you previously had a different team open in settings. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to cancel and restore your previous state.

<Aside type="tip">
Try it: open any ticket, press <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>, type "board", pick **"Board settings"**. The board picker shows that ticket's board and preselects the right team.
</Aside>

## Hiding and Showing Columns
To hide a column using the Command Palette:

1. Open the Command Palette: <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>
2. Type "hide" to find the "Hide column" action
3. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to hide the active (hovered/last-clicked) column directly
4. The Command Palette closes automatically after execution

To show previously hidden columns:

1. Open the Command Palette: <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>
2. Type "show" to find the "Show columns" action
3. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to reveal all hidden sections

<Aside type="note">
"Hide column" now targets the last clicked or currently hovered section rather than cycling through sections, making it easier to hide the specific column you're working with. The "Empty columns" command also reads the current state and filters both the Kanban view groups and the table view groups, showing "Show empty columns" when they're hidden and "Hide empty columns" when they're visible.
</Aside>

An empty view keeps its visible columns on screen, even when empty columns are hidden. Your saved setting does not change. Add a ticket and the other empty columns hide again. Columns you hid individually stay hidden.

## Board palette
Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd> (Windows/Linux) or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd> (Mac) to show the board palette overlay. On the left rail, the board palette displays your user account row with:
- **Email or handle** - Click to open the account switcher dialog
- **Avatar** - Click to open Account & Profile settings

This provides quick access to switching workspaces or reviewing your account configuration without leaving the current board.

<Aside type="tip">
The board palette joins <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> as a non-intrusive way to access workspace settings while staying in context.
</Aside>

## Open Latest Updates
Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> (Windows/Linux) or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> (Mac) then search for **"Latest Updates"** in the board palette or command palette to open the Latest Updates panel from any route in the app. This provides quick access to see recent activity across your boards without leaving your current view.

## Global Alt+Number board shortcuts
**Before:** On the table view or any board view, <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>1-7</kbd> shortcuts did nothing even when the app-shell rail was supposed to be active, causing them to behave as no-ops.

**After:** When the rail is enabled, <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>2-7</kbd> now correctly switch to their corresponding surfaces (Board = 2, Table = 3, Calendar = 4, AI Chat dock = 5, and Search = 6) from any view. On Mac, the global board switcher uses <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>2-7</kbd> instead of <kbd>Cmd</kbd> to avoid interfering with tab switching.

<Aside type="note">
The app-shell rail and global Alt+Number shortcuts were designed to provide tactile, one-hand navigation across main surfaces. Enabling the rail (via account menu or command palette) unlocks these skips so they work reliably everywhere, not only on the rail itself.
</Aside>

## Time reports quick-log
Quick-log time directly from the board or a task card using <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>:

- **On a board or task card** - Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> to open the quick-log dialog preconfigured for the selected card.
- **On an open ticket** - Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> to instantly jump to the per-ticket time log modal, skipping the intermediate step of selecting the ticket from the board list.

The quick-log interface supports Hours and Minutes fields, board and user filters per entry, and works across time zones with per-entry local-noon timestamps for accurate log association with the logged day.

**Keyboard shortcuts**:

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Quick-log time on a selected board card | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> |

## Timer shortcuts
Time tracking shortcuts are available when time tracking is enabled for your board or task:
- **App shell rail** - Press <kbd>7</kbd> on the rail to open the running-timers view
- **Task detail** - Press <kbd>Option</kbd> + <kbd>T</kbd> or <kbd>Alt+T</kbd> to start or stop the open task timer

The timer indicator appears in the task card and task detail, showing whether a timer is running for that task.

See the <a href="/features/time-tracking/">Time Tracking</a> page for full details.

## System-theme prediction
When you open the Command Palette with <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> (or <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd> on Mac), theme-related options now display context-appropriate labels to make system-theme mode predictable. Retired numeric theme modes (1-5) redirect safely to the Appearance settings with your in-session command state preserved.

<Aside type="tip">
Theme options in the command palette now adapt to your system theme and gracefully redirect legacy theme choices to Appearance settings.
</Aside>

## Copy current page URL
When you open the Command Palette with <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd>, the action **"Copy current page URL"** copies the complete browser address, including the board, view, task, filters, and section. The action is available everywhere <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> opens, including task detail, calendar, and inbox views.

<Aside type="note">
The action is available to everyone.
</Aside>

## Use everywhere, including Settings
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> (Windows/Linux) or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> (Mac) now opens the Command Palette on every signed-in page. This includes:
- Boards, tickets, inbox, and search (existing behavior)
- My Tasks view
- All settings pages, such as Settings & General, Board general, and Appearance

On Mac, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> also works in addition to <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>.

Public/sign-in pages, including the sign-in page, still ignore this shortcut.

Escape behavior in Settings:
- First <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the command menu and keeps you in Settings
- A second <kbd>Esc</kbd> exits Settings as usual

This makes the command palette consistently available for board actions, views, and shortcuts throughout the app.

## Mobile in-app gestures
- On mobile, press and hold a comment to open the Command Center with comment actions at the top. Edit comment is first when you wrote the comment.
- Dictation remains the primary input method on mobile; Tap *Improve with AI* to refine your comments without leaving the input flow

## Mobile page exit gesture
On mobile, pressing **<kbd>Esc</kbd>** in the full-screen Pages view now exits via the back action - just like other views in the app. With text typed but unsaved, <kbd>Esc</kbd> clears the unsaved draft. Without text, a single <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the page and stays on the task.

## Ctrl+J board chip
When you press <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd>, the new task box shows which board the task will land on, using the same board chip UI as the AI chat box. The chip appears as soon as the box opens, on every page: a board, a ticket, the inbox and views that mix boards. On a board or ticket page it shows that page's board.

**Board selection logic:**

- **Focused ticket's board:** If a ticket is visible and focused in the inbox, <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd> places the new task on that ticket's board.
- **Open board split:** If there's no focused ticket, the task goes on the open board split.
- **All or Important:** If no board is in context, <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd> uses All or Important as a default board.

Click the chip before saving to change the board.

<Aside type="tip">From the inbox, <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd> is the fastest way to start a new task on a specific board without exiting the feed.</Aside>

## Sending from the Ctrl+J new task box
The new task box sends with the same shortcut as comments and descriptions, so Enter is free for paragraphs.

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Send the new task | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Enter</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Enter</kbd> |
| Start a new paragraph | <kbd>Enter</kbd> | <kbd>Enter</kbd> |

The hint under the box names the shortcut. One press creates one task with everything you typed, and your note stays in the box if the task fails.
### New Task board shortcut hint

Hover over the board chip in **New Task** to see its keyboard shortcut:
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd> on Windows and Linux,
or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd> on Mac.

shortcut to choose a board. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to cancel without losing
your draft.

title: Billing & Seat Management
description: Add and manage seat licenses, view cost forecasts, and test billing flows safely.
---


Hypertask billing controls license capacity, seat limits, and access tiers. Manage seats, track costs, and safely test billing changes in production without risking database side effects.

## Your billing label in Stripe

Stripe uses your team name as the display name on invoices and in the billing portal. Hypertask never shows internal IDs or the word "undefined". For customers without a team name in the app, the owner's email appears instead. Previously blank or malformatted names are now filled from the team name or owner email; customers that have neither team name nor matching owner remain blank.

> Verify customer names in your Stripe billing portal. If a name appears blank, check that its owning team has a name and that a matching owner email exists.

## Seats

Seats represent active users with individual access to Hypertask. Each seat corresponds to a user with login credentials and full access to the platform features.

**Seat limits by plan:**
- Free plan: Unlimited members and unlimited open tickets. You can own up to 3 boards. Archived boards are not counted. A paid or comped plan has no board limit.
- Paid and team plans: Active seat limits per plan
- Enterprise: Custom seat limits

When you create or add accounts, new seats are allocated automatically. Upgrading your paid plan increases your seat capacity; unrestricted reassignments are tracked for billing reconciliation.

## Cost forecasting

The cost forecast shows estimated consumption for GitHub repositories connected to Hypertask. This view helps you anticipate file storage and integration costs before they hit your budget.

**View your forecast:**
1. Go to the **Cost Forecast** page
2. See per-repository estimates broken down by usage type
3. Compare projections against your current subscriptions

## Testing billing changes safely

Stripe test-mode harness lets you safely test billing flows in production without risking database writes or production incidents.

The test harness:
- Runs **guarded seat billing logic** in a controlled environment
- Uses **in-memory application state** so tests don't affect live data
- Implements **bounded cleanup** to discard test states after execution
- **Never writes to the Hypertask database** during test runs

This means you can safely iterate on seat-loss logic, billing entitlement checks, and upgrade/downgrade flows in production-like conditions without creating cross-tenant leakage or corrupting live seats.

## Seat loss and automatic repair

Automatic repair of lost seats is available in production for affected teams. This feature prevents silent seat loss when users pool in from other teams, and helps maintain billing accuracy.

**How automatic repair works:**
- Detects when active teams have fewer seats than their current plan supports
- Verifies that the team has a valid Stripe payment method on file
- Requires billing-owner input if the active subscription cannot identify a single safe replacement Stripe item, to avoid modifying the wrong subscription item
- Blocks automatic repair and prompts for billing-owner review if:
  - A Stripe item is stored but no longer valid
  - The active subscription does not contain exactly one safe replacement at the stored price
  - Automatic selection could modify the wrong subscription item

Only teams with a payment method on file are eligible for automatic repair, and repair operations are guarded against unsafe mutations to subscriptions.

## License management

Seat allocation follows consistent rules across surfaces:

- New user creation adds a seat to your allocation
- Adding teammates in the app, via CLI, or through API all respect the same capacity checks
- Free plan members are unlimited
- Upgrading your plan increases your tracked capacity and adds seats automatically within the new tier bounds

## Team ownership verification

All billing-affected endpoints now verify team ownership server-side before performing mutations:

| Endpoint | Change |
|----------|--------|
| Checkout session creation | Verifies the authenticated user has billing access to the team before creating a checkout URL |
| Task mutations | Reads billing authority from the authenticated user and enforces access checks before state changes |
| Comment operations | Validates the requesting user's access to the target board and task before posting |

This prevents client-controlled parameter mismatches from bypassing authorization and ensures operations are scoped only to the intended team's resources.

## Stripe customer operations

Stripe customer creation for new accounts now surfaces all errors rather than silently swallowing them. Previously, certain paths returned null on failure without indicating the underlying issue, making debugging difficult. All customer creation paths now properly report errors to help you identify and resolve account or payment configuration problems.
