--- title: Scheduling description: Start dates, repeating tasks, task templates, and the My tasks planning view. --- # Scheduling Plan when work starts, set up recurring tasks, or reuse common task structures. Scheduling features help you align work with deadlines, keep deliverables on track, and streamline repetitive project workflows. ## Due dates Set when a task should be completed: - **Pick a date**: Click the due date field on a task or in the New task form, then choose from the calendar. - **Predictive phrases**: Enter phrases like "tomorrow," "next week," or "in 3 days" to set relative dates. - **Remove a due date**: Click today's date or select "No due date" to clear it. ### Snoozed tasks in My Tasks To temporarily hide a task from your My Tasks list, set a snooze until a specific date: - Open the task and use the snooze option in the edit panel, or - Use the command palette (Ctrl + K) and search for "Snooze this task" - The task will no longer appear in My Tasks until that date passes - The snooze date sets a calendar reminder so you can resurface the task later A snooze is per task and independent of other views. Tasks remain otherwise accessible from boards, calendars, and saved views. ### Grouping by due time My Tasks lists tasks by due time by default: - **Overdue**: Due dates in the past, always at the top - **Today**: Due date is today - **This week**: Due date is within the next 7 days - **Later**: Due date is any time in the future - **No due date**: Tasks without a set due date Use the **Group** toggle or saved view settings to show board groups instead. ## My Tasks planning view The **My Tasks** view gives you a personal planning dashboard for work assigned to you: - Groups by due time (Overdue, Today, This week, Later, No due date) - Full Kanban board filters available across all time groups - Custom columns you've defined on your boards are preserved in My Tasks - Real-time live updates: rows refresh automatically when changes happen from other tabs, the CLI, or agents, without reloading the page - Quick-add at the top: type a task title and press Enter to create a task on the view's default board, assigned to you ### Saved views Save custom filters, sorting, board selection, and hidden columns to create personalized My Tasks views: - **Full filtering**: Filter by title, assignee, priority, due date, labels, and more - **Sorting**: Sort by any of the same fields, with priority as the primary sort key - **Board selection**: Show tasks from one board or across multiple boards - **Done columns hidden by default**: Keep focused on active work Behavior change Saved views now use the same save, reset, and Ctrl+K picker flows that you use on the Kanban board for deep controls. The Scope button (including Involvement, Detail, and Group scope) and its corresponding command now open the consistent board picker panel you see throughout the app, with search and standard keyboard navigation for "up to scope" actions. This keeps your palette familiar across inbox and board surfaces. > **Tip**: Create a My Tasks saved view to align on active priorities; at any time you can reorder the view's filters, sorting, or board selection without losing them. Saved views persist at the account level and can be reused or deleted from the view toolbar. ## Repeating tasks Configure a task to repeat on a schedule: - Set a due date and enable repeat - Choose a frequency (daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly) - Specify repeat until (date or count) When a repeat task is marked complete, a new instance appears with the next due date. ## Task templates Task templates save task structures for reuse: - Create a template from a completed task's fields, due date, and subtasks - Apply templates to new tasks to keep formatting consistent - Manage templates from the Board Settings or task detail "Templates" section ## Start dates A start date records when work is *meant to begin*, separately from the due date that records when it must *finished*. **To set one:** open a task, press Ctrl+K, run **Set start date**. The field accepts natural language — `today`, `tomorrow`, `next week monday`, `in 3 days` — or pick from the presets. Choose **Reset** to clear it. The task detail shows a **Start date** row only once the field is set; a task without one looks exactly as it did before. A start date on its own never makes a task overdue. Only a missed *due date* does that. A task that started last week but has no deadline is current work, not late work, and **My tasks** files it accordingly. ### API ```http POST /api/tasks/setStartDate Content-Type: application/json { "taskId": 1234, "startDate": "2026-08-10T09:00:00.000Z" } ``` Pass `"startDate": null` to clear it. Returns the updated task. Requires membership of the task's board. ## Repeating tasks A repeating task recreates itself when you finish it. **To set a repeat:** open a task, press Ctrl+K, run **Repeat task**, and choose a cadence: | Cadence | Meaning | |---|---| | `Daily` | Every day | | `Weekdays` | Every weekday, Monday to Friday | | `Weekly` | Every 7 days | | `Biweekly` | Every 14 days | | `Monthly` | Same day each month, clamped to the last day of shorter months (31 Jan → 28 Feb) | Choose **Don't repeat** to stop a task repeating. The option only appears when a rule is already set. A repeating task shows a **Repeats** row in the task detail. ### What "finishing" means The next occurrence is created when you **move the task into a done column**, or **archive it yourself**. It carries over the title, description, priority, size, labels and assignees, with the date advanced by one period. Two cases deliberately do *not* create a new occurrence: - **Auto-archive.** A board's auto-archive sweep fires because nobody touched a task, which is abandonment rather than completion. Repeating there would regenerate neglected tasks indefinitely. - **Moving the task to another board**, including into that board's done column. Relocating work is not completing it. Finishing a repeating task late never produces an already-overdue copy: the next date is rolled forward until it is genuinely in the future, keeping the original time of day and, for weekly rules, the original weekday. If a board has no column that counts as "not done", the task does not repeat — the new occurrence would otherwise be created directly into a done column, where it would read as finished work the moment it appeared. ### API ```http POST /api/tasks/setRecurrence Content-Type: application/json { "taskId": 1234, "recurrence": "Weekly" } ``` Valid values: `Daily`, `Weekdays`, `Weekly`, `Biweekly`, `Monthly`, or `null` to stop repeating. Requires membership of the board. ## Task templates A template stores the shape of a task so you can create the same kind of work repeatedly without retyping it. Templates are per board, and capture the **title**, **description**, **priority**, **size** and **labels**. **To save one:** open a task you want to reuse, press Ctrl+K, run **Save task as template**. The template is named after the task title. **To use one:** from the board, press Ctrl+K, run **New task from template**, and pick from the list. The new task is created in the board's first non-done column and opens immediately. Labels that were deleted after the template was saved are skipped rather than failing the creation. ### API ```http GET /api/task-templates?projectId=15 # list a board's templates POST /api/task-templates # { "taskId": 1234, "name": "Weekly review" } DELETE /api/task-templates # { "templateId": 7 } POST /api/task-templates/apply # { "templateId": 7 } ``` `name` is optional on create and defaults to the task's title. All four require membership of the board. ## My tasks **My tasks** answers "what am I working on today" across every board you belong to. The inbox remains the place to triage what arrived; this is the place to plan. **To open it:** G then M, or Ctrl+K and **Go to my tasks**, or visit `/my-tasks`. It shows every open task assigned to you as a **table**, the same table the board uses. By default the sections are due-time groups: **Overdue**, **Today**, **This week**, **Later**, and **No due date**. Overdue stays first. Use **Group** to switch to one section per board. Saved My Tasks views remember that choice. **Ordering puts urgent work first.** In time groups, Overdue is the first section. In board groups, boards that contain overdue tasks sort above boards that do not. Inside a group, overdue tasks lead, then the rest by due date, with undated tasks last. **Cross-board priority sorting.** In any table column, click the column header to sort by that column. Sorts are applied across each board's section, so you can see the highest-priority tasks at the top of the list, ordered by the board's default priority level. **Priority levels.** Tasks across all boards are sorted using the board's real priority levels: No Priority, Urgent, High, Medium, and Low. The sort uses these levels consistently regardless of the board's visual cues. **The split pills filter by board.** They still work inside a time group. "All" shows every board; picking a board narrows the table to that board alone. Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through them, exactly as on the inbox and board surfaces. **Sorting keeps the grouping.** Clicking a column header sorts within each time or board section rather than flattening everything into one list. Navigation matches the inbox and scheduled views: J and K (or the arrow keys) to move, Enter to open, Esc to go back. My tasks is a planning surface across every board you belong to. Use the quick-add row at the top to create a task on the view's default board (My Tasks asks once if none is set), or create from a board, the inbox, or Ctrl+K. ## Agent scheduling and provider selection

--- title: Tasks description: Create, assign, and manage tasks with rich fields, priorities, relations, and subtasks. --- --- title: "Tasks" description: "Create, assign, and manage tasks with rich fields, priorities, relations, and subtasks." --- # Tasks A task represents a unit of work that can be assigned, progressed, and tracked. It supports rich fields, priority levels, relationships, and subtasks. ## My Tasks **My Tasks** is your personal task list across boards. By default it shows tasks assigned to you. The list groups by due time: **Overdue**, **Today**, **This week**, **Later**, and **No due date**. Overdue stays at the top. Use **Group** to switch back to board groups. Saved My Tasks views remember the choice. One row of tabs sits on top, your saved views. Use **Scope** to narrow the list to some boards, and **Group: Board** to see one section per board with its count. ### Scope in My Tasks Improvement The **Scope** button in My Tasks and the standard **Scope** command in Ctrl+K now open the same board picker list. The panel has been redesigned to match the board picker you use throughout the app, with search and standard keyboard navigation for quick filtering and selection. The previous, custom implementation has been replaced with the consistent board picker experience. ### Bulk selection and actions on My Tasks You can select multiple tasks in the **My Tasks** view using the keyboard shortcut **G**, followed by **M**, to enter multi-select mode. This mirrors the selection behavior from the Kanban board for a consistent workflow. Once in multi-select mode: - **Verify your selection**: Each task you want to act on is checked. If viewing a filtered list, only tasks that are both checked and visible are included in the action. - **Apply bulk actions**: The following actions are available at the bottom of the list: - Archive - Assign - Label - Move to column - Delete - **Unselect**: Press **G** again or press **U** to exit multi-select mode. Selected rows persist until you commit an action, so you can review the working set before bulk-actioning multiple tasks. > **Tip**: The selection model matches the way you select tasks in Kanban, so if you are comfortable bulk-archiving or moving tasks on a board, the pattern transfers directly to My Tasks. ### Tasks you're snoozed on To temporarily hide tasks from your My Tasks view, set a **snooze**. When you snooze until a date: - The task no longer appears in My Tasks until that date passes - The snooze date sets a calendar reminder so you can resurface the task later A snooze is per task and independent of other views. Tasks remain otherwise accessible from boards, calendars, and saved views. ### Saved views You can create and manage saved views on My Tasks to customize what you see. These views support: - **Full filtering**: Filter by title, assignee, priority, due date, labels, and more. Filter options match the Kanban board filter menu, so you can use familiar screen-level controls directly on My Tasks. - **Sorting**: Sort by any of the same fields, with priority as the primary sort key. - **Board selection**: Show tasks from one board or across multiple boards. - **Done columns hidden by default**: Done columns are hidden within each view to focus on active work. Saved views persist at the account level and can be used as templates for board filter setups. ### How it works When you toggle a filter, sort order, or board, your selection is saved with the view. The next time you open that view, the settings are applied automatically. You can create multiple views for example, one for active prioritized tasks, one for a specific project, or any combination that matches your workflow. To create a saved view, open My Tasks and use the view toolbar to pick filters and sorting options, then select **Save view**. The view appears in the saved views list alongside system views like **Involvement** and **All tasks**. ### Excluding tasks you don't need To hide distracting or temporary tasks: - Use **View filters** to show or hide assignments, priorities, or tags that don't match your current focus. - Create and pin a custom view with the exact criteria you want to see. - Review tasks by tag or priority and archive or move them away when no longer relevant. > **Note:** Saved views are scoped to the current team. Cross-board filters and sorting are supported, so you can see, for example, all high-priority inbox tasks across all boards in a single custom view. ### All Tasks view The **All Tasks** view provides an at-a-glance overview of every active task across the board. It builds split views for each board section (To Do, In Progress, Done, etc.) from a single source of truth. To access this view, navigate to the board and select **All Tasks** from the view toolbar. ### How All Tasks works All Tasks uses a single fetch pass that loads rows once and builds board splits from those rows. As a result: - Each board sees its own split of the task list. - Quiet boards do not lose splits in favor of busy boards. - The view is stable and deterministic across sessions. ### Drawing from multiple streams Since All Tasks is board-wide, it aggregates tasks from all active columns and sections, making it useful for a quick health check or high-level tracking when you need to see everything that matters—not just what's pinned or currently in one section. **Note:** Unlike **My Tasks** saved views, All Tasks does not automatically filter out onboarding, demo, template, and staging content, so those tasks may appear in the list. For visibility filtering, see [Board & Subtask Visibility](/features/board-visibility/). ### Search filters When searching within a board or in saved views, you can now narrow results using search operators on fields: - **from:** Restrict to tasks created by a specific user. - **assignee:** Restrict to tasks assigned to a specific person. - **in:** Restrict to tasks in a board, section, or column. - **label:** Restrict to tasks with a specific label. - **is:** Narrow by task type; for example, `is:card` to show only standard cards. - **dates:** Show tasks with dates matching a condition (by default, **by due**), or filter by due date ranges. - `dates:2026-09-30` For tasks with that exact due date. - `dates:<2026-09-30` For tasks due before. - `dates:>2026-09-30` For tasks due after. - `dates:in-range 2026-09-01..2026-09-30` For tasks due within the range. - `dates:overdue` For tasks marked overdue. - `dates:today` For tasks due today. - `dates:this-week` For tasks due within the current week. - `dates:later` For tasks due later than the current week. - `dates:todays` For tasks due on today and the day prior. - **has:** Show tasks that have a value in a field; for example, `has:due-date` for tasks that have a due date (including empty values) or `has:assignee` for tasks that have someone assigned. - Combining multiple operators is supported—for example, `from:alice label:urgent dates:>2026-09-30` to find urgent tasks created by Alice after a certain date. To apply search filters: 1. Open **Kanban** or **Table View**. 2. On the board header (or in the saved view toolbar), select **Filter**. 3. Choose a field and an operator, then enter a value or pick from the options. 4. Repeat for additional filters to narrow the list. Search filters apply at the board level in Kanban and in saved views. The available operators depend on the board's configuration. ### Chips in the search bar New The search bar includes: - **Chips**: Select or refine filters after your search, then click to apply chips. Click the × on a chip to remove it. - @ people picker: Start typing the @ symbol to select or create people. - # board picker: Start typing # to select or create boards. ## My Tasks toolbar Behavior change The My Tasks toolbar now uses icon-only controls with tooltips for Involvement, Columns, Scope, Filters, Sort, and Group. Active controls turn blue like Kanban, and Group shows its current choice. Overdue tooltips on red counts now appear over each overdue item. The toolbar also uses the same Save view and Reset controls as Kanban board views. From the **Ctrl+K** command palette, you can still use **Save view as** to create a saved view, and **Reset view** to revert My Tasks to its default set of built-in filters. Keyboard shortcuts like **Ctrl+S** and **Ctrl+R** no longer open popovers on the board; they now open the Save view and Reset dialogs respectively. This change makes view management across My Tasks and other board views more consistent, and ensures My Tasks mirrors the primary board interface. ## Creating a task From a board or inbox, click **New task** (or use the keyboard shortcut **Ctrl+N** / Cmd+N). This opens the task creator with the following top-level sections: - **Title**: The name or headline of the work. - **Description**: Optional text explaining what to do. - **Assignees**: One or more members to get notified and held accountable. - **Sections & Columns**: Drag the task to a section or use the section picker dropdown. - **Due date**: Pick a date or use predictive phrases like "tomorrow," "next week," or relative periods. - **Priority**: Choose Low, Medium, or High. - **Estimated time**: Optionally specify hours or a low-high range if needed. Use **Write with AI** (**Ctrl+K** / Cmd+K, or the command palette) in the description area to turn a brief task idea into a fleshed-out task. ### New Task creator New The task creator window (formerly the "Compose" button) can be opened from any view with **Ctrl+J** / Cmd+J and is now live for everyone. The window behaves like a task creator with Search and New Task tabs, Ctrl+K and Ctrl+J tooltips, and Tab/Shift+Tab switching. It retains your old window size and grows as you type, and the New Task button is renamed to **New Task**. On desktop, click the primary **New Task** plus button in the left sidebar to open the same window. Expand the sidebar to see its label. Hover shows **Ctrl+J**, or **Cmd+J** on Mac. Mobile keeps its existing new-task button. ### Edit a task with AI New Click **Edit with AI** under a task's description to open the AI chat in the sidebar on that task. It asks "How do you want to edit this task?" and offers ready-made requests: **Rewrite in plain words**, **Shorten the title**, **Add acceptance criteria**, **Split into sub-tasks**, and **Turn the error log into steps to reproduce**. Pick one or type your own, and the chat updates the task in place. The AI button in the description and comment editor opens the same chat. On an open task, **Ctrl+J** / Cmd+J still opens the New Task window. ### AI writer failure reasons Fix When the AI writer fails to generate a task, the **Ctrl+J New Task** box and the AI Task Writer now show the real failure reason instead of hiding it; your note is still saved as a task. If AI generation is not available, the text you entered appears without modification. This applies to task creation from boards, the inbox, and description editing in task details. ## Field validation Some fields are type-checked before submission. For example, the **ranking** parameter must be a string; passing a number will fail with an error. ## OAuth connection flow When Hypertask connects to a board from an external site or app, Hypertask now shows an **approve screen** first. The screen names the connector and the exact site that will receive access, letting you confirm before any access is granted. This prevents a signed-in user from inadvertently granting external sites access to their entire board without prior approval. ## Managing task details Open a task to view and edit all its fields. Unsupported columns or fields may be hidden based on your team's board configuration. ### Priorities Assign a clear priority (Low, Medium, or High) to reflect the task's importance and replacement cost. Higher priorities should be shown ahead of lower ones in lists, table view, and filters. ### Assignees - Added assignees trigger notifications to the task's assignees. If no assignee is specified, the task is unassigned. - Workers can have their own assignee field, tracked separately from human assignees. Workers appear in the Relationships section under the *Workers* relation type. ### Due dates Click a date to pick another date or remove it. The date affects due date pickers and filter views. Predictive phrases like "tomorrow," "next week," and relative periods also persist. ### Estimated time Type hours or a low-high range for time-tracking integration. ### Section & column Drag tasks between sections to change their column. This can trigger auto-assign rules if configured. In Table view, you can also drag any row onto another section's card; the row is the drag handle, the section card is the drop target, and the change surfaces immediately in both views (Column sort must be off for this to work; on /my-tasks, rows are grouped by time or board, so dragging doesn't target a section directly). ### Description edition UX To edit the task description: - On desktop: Click or tap the description area, then edit. - Mobile: Double-tap the description to open the editor; a single tap remains in read mode. If you are the **Task Reporter** (see below), you can edit the description directly. Only the Task Reporter can edit the description. ### Task Reporter With the **Task Reporter**, anyone on the task can update the task description directly. The Task Reporter indicator visually appears alongside comment headers, making it clear who has opened the description for editing just like comments. ### Permissions - **Task Reporter** is available to any human assignee or worker on a task. The feature is not available for closed tasks. - When you open the description in edit mode, you become the **Task Reporter** for that task. - Only the Task Reporter can edit the description. This prevents concurrent edits and restores the semantic meaning of "owner of the description field". - If you close the description without saving any changes, the status clears and the next person to open it becomes the Task Reporter. This model ensures a clear ownership of the description field, similar to comment ownership, which helps teams coordinate around tasks without stepping on each other's work. Note: While you are the Task Reporter, you cannot switch to another task description edit until the current edit state closes, preserving a single active description edit at a time. ### Saved attachments - To remove an attachment, open the description in edit mode, click the attachment you want to remove, and save. Only the items you deselect will be removed; remaining attachments are preserved as one copy each. Fix A previous bug caused the wrong attachment files to be saved when removing items from a description. When you had two or more description files attached, removing one would incorrectly save a duplicate of the other file. This is now fixed so that always only one copy of each remaining attachment is saved. Fix Deleting a task no longer creates an invalid undoable state. Undo is now always possible when restoring from deletion, ensuring tasks can be fully recovered and the undo system behaves consistently. Fix Undo functionality has been consolidated under a single restoring rule. This ensures that restoring tasks after deletion behaves the same whether you use the Undo button or Ctrl+Z, with consistent behavior tracked through the board's undo history. ### Agent lease interactions When you make manual changes to a task—"moving, assigning, unassigning, archiving, or deleting"—Hypertask cancels any active agent lease on that task and persists the change. Human modifications take priority over agent tasks, but agent-versus-agent collision protection remains in place. This ensures your task updates are never blocked by an agent while you're working. ## Task detail view Open a task to see: - Header with title, status section, assignees, workers, priority, and due date. - Description area with optional attachments. - Sections: Comments, Relations, Subtasks, Times, and Pages. - Task Reporter indicator marking who can edit the description. - **Top bar** with instant navigation and actions: - ← **Back to task** — Settings-style back button for navigation. On mobile, the back control matches the app's mobile back style with normal side spacing, making it easy to tap and fully visible up to 390px wide. - **Save** — Only right-aligned action remaining in the top bar; **Delete** is now moved to the **Undo** action in the Actions section. ### Linked pull requests Tasks can link to GitHub pull requests. The pull request section displays each linked PR with its status: - **Open, Merged, Closed**: Show the current status as reported by GitHub. - **Last observed**: The last-known status before the page loads. - **Fetching...**: Indicates a background refresh is in progress. Improvement Tasks with linked PRs now show any saved PR status immediately—Open, Merged, or Closed—without waiting for GitHub to respond. Queries to GitHub run in parallel in the background and update the panel once the fetch completes, keeping the page fast and responsive. If you navigate away and come back, the PR panel refreshes again to stay current. This change eliminates wait times for tasks with linked PRs and provides an instant-open experience even when GitHub fetches are slower than usual. Security Hypertask now verifies that incoming PR updates come from known GitHub accounts before accepting them. By default, this restriction applies only to board 15. Except for board 15, an updated PR can link to any public repository, and the update is accepted as long as it originates from a trusted GitHub account. For board 15, only PR updates from three specified accounts are permitted: Valentin Yeo and two others configured by the board team. This prevents unauthorized actors from creating, moving, or commenting on tasks in board 15 via external PRs. ### Comments The comment thread shows all comments on the task. By default, when you open a task with comments, the newest comment remains expanded so you can see the latest conversation. Link handling Plain web addresses in ticket descriptions and comments (http:// or https://) are automatically transformed into clickable links. Detects addresses based on recognized URL patterns, ensuring links in work notes and teammate discussions remain navigable on both desktop and mobile. Performance improvement When you open a task, comments now load once instead of twice. The initial SSR data used as the starting point, with React Query configured to skip a second fetch if the data is fresh. This eliminates redundant data handling and speeds up task loads: repeat visits are now approximately 0.6 seconds faster. New and edited comments still appear automatically without a reload, and realtime invalidation, reconnect reconciliation, and window-focus refresh continue to work as expected. Improvement Long task pages and comment threads now send their initial snapshot only once, reducing data copies and decoding passes. Repeat visit times drop from roughly 2.2 seconds to about 0.6 seconds. The change applies to tasks with many comments or long descriptions and focuses on the initial load speed, preserving all existing behavior for navigation, real-time updates, and comment handling. Fix The comment box on ticket pages is now positioned immediately below the last comment instead of appearing in the middle of the task. It previously moved under the task description, causing the interface to split the comment content unnaturally. The comment section now renders after other content and before the top bar, keeping comments at the bottom of the page as expected. Fix A shared comment link now opens on that comment instead of the ticket top, with the comment visible on screen on both desktop and mobile. The link scrolls directly to the referenced comment when you open it—for example, from Slack or email—making it easier to reference specific points in a conversation. This fix improves navigation for long threads with hundreds of comments and helps ticket descriptions stay readable even on narrow phones. ### Actions Common actions include: - **Back**: Navigate back to the board using the ← Back to task button. - **Move**: Relocate the task to a different section, board, or project. - **Duplicate**: Create a copy with the same fields. When duplicating a task, the new task includes the full description and can be copied to another board in one step (see board-level Duplicate in the [Boards & Sections](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/boards/) docs). - **Archive**: Hide the task from current views while keeping it in the archive. - **Delete**: Permanently remove the task. Undo appears on the notification after deletion, clicking **Undo** restores the task to its previous column and keeps it available for future edits. For bulk deletions, undo restores all affected tasks together and still works with Ctrl / Cmd+Z. Fix Opening a ticket now downloads its details once, and board cards stay up to date. Before this fix, opening a task from the board or by its link would trigger 2 to 3 redundant data fetches. Fix On mobile, tapping a board card no longer loads the task page twice. The board now shows the task without redundant data fetches, eliminating a flash or stutter that previously occurred. This fix applies across all boards and resizes, keeping the board-tap experience smooth. Security Tasks can link to GitHub pull requests. Board 15 now accepts automatic PR updates only from three known GitHub accounts: Valentin Yeo and two others configured by the board team, preventing outsiders from creating tasks, moving them to review, or commenting via PRs. Security A person who is not on a board can no longer add labels to it or modify label assignments on tasks. Outsiders now receive a Forbidden error, while board members continue to manage labels as before. Security A team-only share link no longer exposes task content to outsiders. Before, the page sent the whole task and comments to unauthenticated users who only saw blurred content. Now an outsider sees an empty page with a Sign in or Login bar and cannot see task details or comments. Security When you attempt to move or nest a task under another task on an inaccessible board, the operation is refused and nothing is saved. Hypertask validates board boundaries before allowing parent-child relationships across unrelated teams, preventing accidental exposure of foreign task titles or context. ## Relations between tasks Create relationships between tasks to surface context without leaving tasks: - **Block**: Mark a task as blocking another task. - **Blocked by**: Identify what indirectly holds a task back. - **Duplicate**: Link to other tasks that represent the same work item. - **Workers**: Associate an agent or intelligent agent with the task for scheduling and coordination. See a task's relations in the **Relations** section of the task detail view. ## Subtasks Break down a task into smaller units. Subtasks appear in the task detail under the **Subtasks** section. Mark them complete to show progress toward the parent task. Add one from the parent task's **Subtasks** section. The window lists tasks you can link as a sub-task, and the **New sub-task** button under the search box opens the normal create window with the parent already attached. Typing a name that matches nothing still creates a new sub-task when you press Enter. ## Task property rail The task detail sidebar includes a rail of properties (title, priority, assignees, labels, etc.). The rail now occupies the full remaining dynamic viewport height, so it uses all available space rather than a fixed maximum and leaves no unused viewport space. **Task properties no longer scroll with the task thread**, keeping them pinned to the sidebar for easy access while browsing comments and history. When another browser, the CLI, or an agent changes a task, its open detail page refreshes the title, assignees, labels, priority, dates, status, attachments, and linked pull requests without a reload. If the live connection is unavailable, the page checks for changes every 10 seconds. ## Time tracking Track work hours on tasks via the **Times** section: - **B** opens the time entry modal from the task, or use the command palette ("Log time"). - Manual per-day rows let you log time for any calendar day without a timer. - Export time logs as CSV for payroll or reporting. See the [Time Tracking](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/time-tracking/) guide for full details. ## AI Task Writer The AI Task Writer is a prompt-based task creation flow that generates complete, shippable tickets from paste inputs. ### How it works today The Task Writer writes tasks in your team's style. It uses board-aware prompts, pulls task templates from boards, and uses search to find related tickets instead of inventing them. ### Using the Task Writer - From a board: **Ctrl+J** / Cmd+J and select **Create with AI** — **Task Writer**. - From the command palette: **Ctrl+K** — search for "Task Write" and select it. - From a task: Click the AI icon in the task header and select **Task Writer**. After the Task Writer generates a draft, you can refine it just like any other AI-generated comment or description. ### Board task templates Save a representative ticket through **Ctrl+K → Save as template**. Open **Settings → Board → Task templates** to edit its name, title pattern, and description structure. Use names such as **Bug** or **A/B test** so the writer can match your request to the right template. Simple descriptions support headings written with `##` and plain paragraphs. Rich descriptions remain read-only here to preserve their formatting; you can still change their names and title patterns. If someone else saves first, reload before saving your changes. When you explicitly request ideas, the writer fills them in one pass using board tickets, documents, memory, and custom instructions. For example, “Write an A/B test with five headlines” produces five finished headlines, not placeholders. A matched template's title pattern and headings stay in place. Required ICE scores include the component scores and mark estimates. Ordinary editing requests still preserve your source instead of inventing copy. ## Instant ticket opening New Tickets now load instantly from cached board data, with no spinner, no "Loading..." text, and no placeholder animation. The entire opening experience is fast and lag-free across desktop and mobile. ### What you see - **Click to open**: When you tap or click a task, it appears in about 0.15 to 0.3 seconds on both desktop and mobile. - **No loading animation**: No full-screen spinner, no pulsing grey bars, no brief placeholder state. - **Suggested questions right away**: If the AI panel is open, suggested questions appear immediately—not waiting for the API response. ### Browser history The browser back and forward buttons now behave consistently with the app: - Press **Back** to return to the board. The board remains loaded and you can stay there. - Press **Forward** to re-open the last ticket you viewed. This lets you browse through tasks inside the app while the rest of your session stays tight and fast. ### Performance details - Median open times are ~0.15 seconds on desktop and ~0.17 seconds on mobile. - The first open after a board loads takes about 0.25 to 0.33 seconds; subsequent opens are closer to 0.13 to 0.18 seconds. - The first open after a board loads now paints its cached title and description before expensive editing property controls, so the title and description appear instantly while controls like assignees, status, and priority still warm. This tighter paint-first sequence reduces the first-open delta to about 0.10 seconds—considerably faster than before. ### Visual smoothness Fix Ticket pages no longer shift or jitter after opening. Visual elements that previously filled in after the initial paint now appear instantly as part of the cached board data, keeping the title, description, and controls in place across desktop and mobile for all test accounts. ### Keyboard shortcuts We recommend using keyboard shortcuts to navigate: - **Ctrl+J** / Cmd+J to jump to a task or open it with the Task Writer. - **Ctrl+O** / Cmd+O to jump to a task or link from within the task detail. These shortcuts preserve the instant-open feel and keep you moving without page spins or wait states. ### Assignee persistence Improvement When you assign a task from the assign picker, closing the picker or pressing Escape no longer drops the assignment. The human assignee name stays on the task and persists across page reloads and subsequent checks. This applies whether you assign from the board card or from a direct task link. ### Faster task opening Improved Pressing **Back** after opening a subtask now shows the parent task immediately instead of the subtask, with no "Loading..." flash, and **Forward** returns you to the subtask if needed. Opening a task directly from cached data shows it reliably within about 0.3 seconds on both desktop and mobile, eliminating previous delays. ### Navigating to previous titles in Inbox Improved Using **J** or the arrow keys to move to the next Inbox item now loads and displays it within about 0.3 seconds on desktop and mobile, removing lag that previously held up the wrong ticket title for up to several seconds. ### No flash of the ticket title after opening a board card Fixed Pressing **Back** right after opening a board card now shows the board immediately, with no flash of the ticket title. In at least 19 of 20 quick Backs (within 0.3 seconds of opening a card), you see only the board, not the ticket, and the board is visible within 1 second. ### Task detail downloads once Fix Opening a ticket now downloads its details once, and board cards stay up to date. Before this fix, opening a task from the board or by its link would trigger 2 to 3 redundant data fetches. ### Board tap loading Fix On mobile, tapping a board card no longer loads the task page twice. The board now shows the task without redundant data fetches, eliminating a flash or stutter that previously occurred. This fix applies across all boards and resizes, keeping the board-tap experience smooth. ### Faster open on cold phone Improved Opening a task on a cold phone with no cached data now shows its title and description sooner (11.8 s vs 14.1 s median, 95th-percentile gap of ~2.3 s). The first load paints the title and description earlier, while controls like assignee and priority still warm up afterward, keeping the experience instant and frictionless. ### Ticket page no longer shifts on mobile Fix The ticket page no longer jumps on first load. The comment box appears once and never moves: 20 of 20 fresh loads on two test accounts, on both desktop and phone. Visual elements that previously filled in after the initial paint now appear immediately as part of the cached board data, keeping the title, description, and controls in place across platforms for all test accounts. ### Comments no longer jump with content Behavior change The comment box and comment thread no longer shift downward as content loads, so the task layout stays consistent across desktop and mobile from open to load. ### Instant board tap New Clicking a board card now initializes the task with a single board interaction instead of triggering redundant rendering. This keeps the opening experience snappy across desktop and mobile, especially after boards have already been reloaded. Loading address-bar updates that occur as part of the navigation are tracked correctly as navigations within the same page rather than distinct page loads. The change applies across all boards and view types—Kanban, table, and card lists—with consistent, performant behavior. ## Invited-in aspects and board validation Improved Pages that use invite links now validate board context before sending requests. **My Tasks** and **Inbox** no longer fire invite-link requests without an associated board, which previously caused console errors for unmatched requests. With this fix, such invalid requests now surface a clear, user-facing message instead of a server error, keeping the console clean and providing explicit feedback when a board context is required.

--- title: AI Agents description: Create, configure, and manage autonomous agents in Hypertask with MCP, webhooks, and scheduled vs ad-hoc workflows. --- Agents are autonomous workers that create, update, and manage tasks on your boards. They run as service accounts with scoped API keys and can act on their own behalf via bearer tokens. ## Create and configure agents Follow [Connect a new agent](/connect-an-agent/) for the full setup: 1. **Create:** In [Agent Chat](https://app.hypertask.ai/agents/chat), choose **+ Add agent**. This creates an agent with no boards and shows its token once. Alternatively, open a team board and use **Ctrl+K > Create agent** with **External** selected. That path adds the agent to the current board and opens its page. 2. **Copy the token:** Save the Chat token before closing the dialog. If you did not copy a token from board-based creation, use **Access key > Regenerate** on the agent page and copy the new token. The access key is for a managed agent's own identity, and connecting your own editor (VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code) uses your personal API key from **Settings** (gear icon) → **Connect** → **MCP** instead ([Authentication](/mcp/overview/#authentication)). 3. **Add boards:** The person who owns the agent opens [Agents](https://app.hypertask.ai/agents), opens the agent, expands **Board access**, and ticks a board they can access. Turn the agent on first if disabled. Changes save immediately. **Board settings > Agents** only lists agents already attached; it has no add control. Private agents are visible only to their owner. An agent can only join boards in its team; the first board establishes that team.
An agent cannot add itself to a board, whatever its role. Admin agents can add other agents of the same owner only on boards they already belong to. Do not promote an agent to admin to onboard it; ask its owner to grant access.
For scripted setup, use the [CLI agent commands](/cli/commands/#hypertask-agents-create). To add a board to an existing agent, run this with the owner's own login, not the agent token or an agent-bound connection: ```bash hypertask agents update --id --add-project ``` Agent invitations need the agent UUID, not its display name. If you open Agent Chat or list a team's agents and that team has none you can see, Hypertask adds a Hyper AI agent on a board of that team so the list is not empty. This also works when you can use the team but are not yet a member of a board. ## Agent status Agent pages show a single, consistent status. When Hyper AI agents are targeted via chat, they reflect **On demand** rather than **Offline**, because Hypertask launches them on demand to handle your request instead of running as background workers that report a status.
Built-in Hyper AI agents are always **On demand** when you message them—their behavior changes from continuous background workers to on-demand launches. This means users won't see a persistent "Offline" status for these agents because they only appear when your conversation activates them.
## Board card agent status New. When you run an agent on a board, a small status chip appears on task cards showing: - **Agent name** — The agent performing the work. - **State** — e.g., "working" when the agent is actively updating tasks. - **Age** — How long since the agent last did something, displayed as "just now," "1m ago," "5m ago," etc. The status updates live with the card data and never triggers an extra request per card. Performance measurements show the chip does not make the board measurably slower.
Watch the status chip on board cards to see how your agents are progressing through tasks in real time.
## Agent reactions New. Agents can receive emoji reactions on their comments. A thumb-up on an agent's comment reaches that agent immediately as a signal of acknowledgment or approval. When you respond with a reaction on an agent's comment (for example, ⬆️ or 👍), Hypertask sends that reaction to the targeted agent within seconds. The reaction appears on the task detail page and in the comment feed, and the agent receives the signal even if you're not both online. Agent reactions work across all platforms: desktop, mobile, and through APIs. The reaction is persistent and visible when you return to the task later.
For security, reactions on agent comments stop counting toward flag-based triggers after the comment is edited.
## Agent notifications Improved. Agent notifications include mentions directed at agents (e.g., "Reply to @dev-bot"). These are handled with special guard-rules to prevent them from being incorrectly archived during snooze or reminder lookups. The system skips reminder validation when the notification is addressed to an agent, ensuring agent rows stay visible until you explicitly take action on them. ### Guest Hyper AI seeded notifications Fresh guest inboxes now receive 4 seeded notifications from a Hyper AI agent. When available, the Important split is enabled, helping new users immediately experience AI-driven prioritization. ### Agent Connected and First Task email messages Improved. Agent notifications now use a shared onboarding email design for: - **Your agent is connected** — Confirmation email when you sign up and connect an agent - **Your first task** — Email when a task is assigned to your newly connected agent These emails mirror your selected theme colors, typography, and layout tokens, so they match the look and feel of other in-boxed notifications. Subscribe to Agent notifications in your account settings or skip them entirely if you prefer list-only delivery. ## Clear refusals for invalid actions Improved. Agents that try to perform invalid or unauthorized actions now receive clear, early refusals instead of server errors. For example, if an agent attempts to archive a Done task that cannot be archived, it receives a specific “not allowed” message rather than a generic [HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error]() response. This makes debugging agent workflows easier and prevents unexpected crashes during bulk operations.
Check error messages from your agents when they're stuck—clear refusals point to permission issues, board and column permissions, or task storage states that limit what actions are available.
## Agent chat polling behavior Improved. Agent Chat now uses a simpler, direct method to check agent status instead of flag-driven polling. The previous feature flag for polling has been removed, and the system uses shorter, more consistent checks. Users experience reliable agent status updates without the hidden switch. ## Writing check Agent comments and new tickets are refused when they use a dashed code name, quote Valentin in plain quote marks, ask a Question in the wrong shape, or leave out Problem, Fix, Done when, Risk, or Decision. People can still write those. Put a code name in the agent log. Put his words in a quote block. A Question starts with What this is, then at most three plain points, then Question, My recommendation, Why, Yes, and No, each on its own line. ## Agent governance All agent activities are logged in the board's activity history. You can view who performed each action, when, and the tasks that were modified. This transparency helps teams audit agent workflows and resolve issues quickly.

--- title: Board Settings description: Manage planning, notifications, auto-archive, staleness detection, time tracking, and per-column auto-assign rules. --- Use board settings to plan one board and control its automatic behavior. Set its target and milestones, post health updates, mute notifications, or configure archival, staleness, time tracking, and assignment rules. ## What this affects Board settings apply to individual boards on a project. They govern default behaviors that are applied consistently across tasks when rules are triggered: - **Archive actions** — Automatically archive old tasks or mark them for archival to keep your board clean. - **Project planning** — Set a target date, track milestones, and post the board's current health. - **Board notifications** — Mute ordinary inbox, email, and push notifications from this board only. - **Staleness rules** — Automatically detect tasks that have been idle for a set period and take action. - **Auto-assign rules** — Set per-column rules so new or unassigned tasks get attention where they belong. - **Time totals** — Optionally show accumulated tracked time on task cards and in table view. - **Synchronized IndexedDB defaults** — For authenticated Board and Table routes, the synchronized IndexedDB read model is now enabled by default to keep data in sync across opened tabs without manual refresh. You can still opt into the local model by using `?local_db=0` in the URL.
Board settings are stored at the board level, so you can tailor behaviors per workflow. Changes here apply immediately; monitor the effect on your active tasks.
## Reach You can open board settings from: - **Ctrl+K command palette** — Search for **"Board settings"** and select your board. The board and team you opened from are now preselected. - **Board menu** — Open a board's menu and choose **Settings**. ```markdown Clear expired backlog and automate housekeeping. Identify tasks that haven't moved recently. Propagate responsibilities to unassigned cards. Keep data in sync across browsers by default for authenticated board and table routes. ``` ## Ticket prefix Each board has a deterministic ticket prefix (e.g., HTPR, YPER4, HYFA). Owners can rename the prefix from board settings without changing existing ticket numbers. Prefixes are 2–5 letters or digits, unique within the team, and appear as live previews. ### How to change a prefix From the app: 1. Open a board. 2. Click **Settings** > **Board** > **General**. 3. Find **Ticket prefix**. 4. Enter a new prefix (2–5 characters, letters or digits) and press Enter. 5. Old ticket IDs continue to resolve, so links, comments, and PRs that reference them stay accurate. From the CLI: ```bash hypertask project update --prefix NEWXY --project 15 ``` The prefix is editable on the **Create board** screen (defaulted to the automatic suggestion) and available to agents via the same `project update --prefix` flag. ### Discovering ticket prefix settings From the command palette, type **"ticket prefix"** to jump to this setting. The search returns **"Settings: Ticket prefix (board)"** for the current board. Use this to quickly locate the prefix configuration when you need to update it. ### Rationale - **Instant updates:** The displayed ID is built from the board's current prefix and the ticket's number, so changing the prefix is a quick update instead of rewriting every ticket. - **Backwards compatibility:** Old ticket IDs keep resolving via aliases, just like old numbers already do. - **Avoid clashes:** Moved tickets take the next free number, so prefixes and numbers never conflict, even after deleting tickets or changing prefixes.
Prefixes are currently limited to these known values: HTPR, YPER4, and HYFA, which are used by existing agents. Changing those prefixes will require updating agent checks accordingly.
## Board notifications Open **Settings → Board → General**, then turn **Board notifications** off to mute one board. The change applies immediately and persists across refreshes. Muting a board stops its ordinary: - Inbox notifications, including snoozed items returning later. - Push notifications. - Immediate and digest emails. - Assignment, reaction, task-move, and due-date alerts. Your global notification channel settings stay unchanged, and other boards continue notifying you. Direct replies from managed agents still appear in your inbox so an explicit agent request can return its answer. Turn **Board notifications** on again whenever you want to resume delivery. ## Project planning Open **Settings → Board → Planning** to keep the board's outcome and current health in one place. - Set the board's **target date**. - Add dated **milestones**, then mark them complete as the project advances. - Post a short health update as **On track**, **At risk**, or **Off track**. - Review the 20 most recent updates with their author and timestamp. Any board member can read planning and post a health update. Only the board owner or an admin can change the target date or milestones. Target and milestone changes save immediately. Press **Ctrl+Enter** or **Cmd+Enter** to post a health update from the message field. ## Auto-archive Configure automatic archival of tasks that no longer require attention. Archive is different from deletion—it keeps history while removing items from the active view so you don't have to manually clean up stale columns. ### Available options Rules you can set per board: - **Enable auto-archive** — Turn the rule on/off. - **Archive after** — Choose how many days tasks remain before archival. - Common presets: 90, 120, 180, 365. - **Archive unused** — Automatically archive tasks that have not been touched recently (see Staleness). ### How it behaves When a task crosses your configured threshold: - The board removes the task from column counts. - Tasks are moved to the board's Archive section. - History (comments, attachments, subtasks) remains intact. Tasks in any column are eligible: backlog, in-progress, review, and so on.
Use the **Archive after** setting on columns you keep as a long-running backlog. Combine with staleness for a two-layer cleanup rule.
## Set a column work limit Use a work limit to spot crowded columns without blocking task moves. 1. Open the board and click a column title. 2. In **Manage board columns**, open that column's settings. 3. Enter a positive whole number in **Work limit**. 4. Leave the field to save the limit. The column count shows active tasks / limit and turns red above the limit. The count includes active tasks hidden by filters. Archived and deleted tasks do not count. You can still create and move tasks when the column is over its limit. Clear **Work limit** to remove the limit. The limit belongs to the column, so saved views share it. ## Staleness detection Staleness rules keep track of active tasks that have not been moved, updated, or interacted with in a defined window. This helps surface forgotten items that might need re-evaluation or removal. Configuration: - **Stale after** — Number of days since the last change/due date. - Suggested ranges: 30, 60, 90. - **Auto-assign stale tasks** (Optional) — Toggle the rule that moves or re-assigns stale tasks to a specific column or assignee. - **Stale reminders** (Optional) — Get notified when tasks reach the staleness threshold so you can prioritize review or cleanup. When staleness is enabled, Kanban cards show the task's age on the board before its age in the current column. Fresh cards show muted ages. Cards become amber at the warning threshold and red at the hot threshold. Use Ctrl+K to toggle staleness for the board or the current view. ### Filtering stale vs healthy Every staleness filter is named so that typing **stale** in the filter menu finds all of them: - **Stale in column** — days since the task last changed column, falling back to its creation date if it has never moved. - **Stale without comment** — days since the last comment, falling back to creation if nobody has ever commented. - **Stale on board** — days since the task was created, regardless of activity (not affected by column moves or comments). - **Not stale** — the inverse: both the column age and the comment age are under the warn threshold. This deliberately ignores board age: a long-lived task that is still being moved and discussed is not stale. All four filters apply the per-board staleness threshold automatically, so a filtered board always agrees with the ages shown on the cards.
Staleness only accounts for updates to the task record. Activities like commenting or toggling status updates the last-touch date automatically.
## Auto-assign rules Define rules that automatically assign or re-assign tasks to specific members. This is useful for ensuring that new pull requests, backlog items, or triage items land with the right people without manual overhead. ### Per-column auto-assign on column move In addition to setting a default for the entire board when a task is created or is unassigned, you can configure a per-column auto-assign rule: whenever a task is moved into this column, it will be assigned to the specified person or group. Ctrl+K "Auto-assign for this column" opens the per-column configuration. To configure per-column auto-assign: 1. From the board or section header, open the context menu (or use Ctrl+K "Auto-assign for this column") and select the section where you want the rule. 2. Pick an assignee (group or individual) to apply as tasks are moved into that column. The assignment is additive and idempotent—moving a task back into another column and then into this column again respects the rule. 3. When the rule applies, all tenants receive a notification and the assignee is messaged in the source channel if notifications are set up for the board. Auto-assign runs within the effective membership and session context enforced for board write access. Use board-visibility gating to control which users gain or retain write access to the board; ID-based attempts outside that context are scoped to the session owner's permissions. ### Calling auto-assign via CLI/MCP When auto-assign is triggered by CLI or MCP tools, the assignee lookup is evaluated in the context of the authenticated user or tool's session. Actions cannot be authorized by leases or background jobs outside that session; approvals are enforced through the board's membership and write-access model. ### How to configure (defaults) - **Target columns** — Specify which columns should apply auto-assign triggers: - Any column that can receive tasks (e.g., In Progress, Review). - **Assign to** — Select a project member or a role-based assignment: - Individual users. - Groups (e.g., "Testers," "Backend team"). - **Optional priority filter** — Apply only to tasks with certain priority levels (e.g., Urgent, High). ### Scenarios - **Backlog channel** — Assign new backlog items to reviewers or maintainers. - **Review overload** — Auto-assign completed items to QA reviewers when they become "In Review". - **Slack alerts** — Combine with board notifications to alert assignees when auto-assign runs.
Pair auto-assign rules with open notifications (e.g., open issue in Slack team) to ensure assignees know their attention is needed without just silently moving cards.
## Autosave drafts Changes to board settings are saved automatically. If you navigate away or refresh the page, your settings persist: - **No manual save needed** — All toggles, number inputs, and column mappings are applied instantly. - **Revert behavior** — If you make a mistake, the board defaults (detected from project/staleness rules) can be used as a backup; update the offending rule and save again. ## Logging and history Hypertask tracks rule executions at the board level for review: - **Rule runs** — Historically, Hypertask logged rule runs to a log table (Admin role visible). - **Rule hygiene** — To keep logs manageable, Hypertask retains only recent rule executions (e.g., last 14–30 days) on the log table, while preserving a full backup in a more extensive repository for administrative use.
Hygiene protects performance and schema stability over time. Project owners should rely on boards and historiques for governance rather than logs after a few days.
## Synced IndexedDB defaults You can choose between two read models for Boards and Tables: - **Synchronized IndexedDB (default)** — Active when no `?local_db=0` in the URL. Keeps data in sync across opened tabs and browsers smoothly, at the cost of higher CPU and a small memory overhead. Use this if you regularly open the same board in multiple tabs or devices. - **Local IndexedDB (optional)** — Activated by appending `?local_db=0` to the URL. Reads and writes stay in the local browser state, giving high performance with less CPU and a smaller footprint. Data may not reflect changes from other tabs or browsers until you reload. This defaults to the synchronized model for authenticated Board and Table routes. The system preserves the opt-out via URL flags, so local flow can still be opted into for testing or performance-sensitive workflows. ## Auto-error routing targeting Bugs When auto-error tickets are routed to sections, Hypertask now targets the exact Bugs section by default instead of the board's default column. This applies globally for boards with a specific Bugs section. Boards without a clearly defined Bugs section fall back to the current default section behavior. Changes take effect after board settings are saved.
If you see Bugs incorrectly routed to another section, double-check that the Bugs section exists with a unique name and that you're using the latest board settings cache after this release.

title: Skills
description: Create, manage, and import skills to organize your team's expertise and filter by them in queries and saved views.
---


Skills let you cluster related tasks, projects, and workflows around shared expertise. A skill can be anything: a domain, a technology, or a role. You can assign skills to people, filter any task list by skill, or use skills as metadata in saved views.

<Aside type="tip">
Use skills to surface specialized work: "React", "Schema Design", "Customer Research", or "Onboarding". Assign a skill to a person, and watch it surface in searches, assignments, and saved views.
</Aside>

## Save a workflow from AI chat

Ask chat to create a skill:

> Turn this session into a skill.

Or describe a workflow you want saved.
Review its name, slug, trigger, instructions and scope.
Choose personal scope or the current board.
Confirm the draft to save it.
Or request edits or reject the draft.
Edits need another preview before saving.
Nothing saves until you confirm the draft.
If the slug exists, approve an update instead.

Use `/slug` in chat, comments, or Task Writer.
Ctrl+J also supports saved skills.

## Create & assign skills

Skills are scoped to: personal (for you), project (for a board), or team (for all members of that team). When you assign a skill to a person, the assignment is also scoped to the skill’s scope, so a team-level skill appears in each project’s skill list.

<Steps>

1. **Open Skill management**
   - Use the **Ctrl+K** command palette and search for **"Skills"**, or go to the **Settings > Skills** page.

2. **Create a skill**
   - Click **New Skill**.
   - Give it a name (e.g., "Python" or "Design System").
   - Optionally add a description.
   - Choose the scope:
     - **Personal** — skill available only to you.
     - **Project** — skill available on a specific board/project.
     - **Team** — skill available to all members of your team, regardless of project.

3. **Assign a person**
   - On the skill card, click **Assign People**.
   - Search for a team member and add them.
   - Assignments are scoped: a personal skill assignment is only visible to you; a project assignment is only visible on that project’s board.

4. **Backlog/assign tasks by skill**
   - Filter a task list by skill using the skill picker.
   - Or assign a skill to a task to tag it for later filtering or reporting.
   - Saved views can also explicitly filter by skill.

</Steps>

## Run a skill from a ticket comment

Start writing a comment on any ticket. Type `/`, then choose an available skill. Use Enter or click to choose the skill.

The AI chat sidebar opens with its answer. The skill reads the ticket and your draft. Your comment stays editable and unposted.

### /prototype skill

You can now create a **/prototype** skill to define a shared prototype format across agents and collaboration tools. When someone inserts a prototype with this skill:

- The prototype becomes clickable in comments and AI chat.
- The default action is to open and display the prototype in the same context.
- The prototype’s slug is inserted into comments and prompts, making it easy to reference and reuse.
- If the prototype has its own action URL, the UI presents standard context‑appropriate actions:
  - **Comment composer**: click the prototype card to insert its slug; opening the prototype works the same way as other skills.
  - **AI chat**: pick /prototype from the command menu, then engage with the prototype in the same way you would any other skill.

<Aside type="tip">
Use the /prototype skill to streamline reference workflows: embed consistent embed URLs and referenceable slugs for MP4s, PNGs, and hosted prototypes. Agents and collaborators can open, inspect, and reference them without leaving their current flow.
</Aside>

### Use a skill when writing a new task

Press **Ctrl+J**, start your note with the skill's slug (for example `/deeper`), and send it. The AI writes the task using that skill, then opens the task with the AI chat.

As soon as you type `/`, a skill picker opens under your cursor, the same one the AI task writer shows. Keep typing to filter it, use the arrow keys to move, and press **Enter** or **Tab** to insert the skill. **Escape** closes only the picker, so your note stays open.

The chat's first message tells you which skill shaped the task and what changed compared with your note. It then lists concerns, ideas and follow-up questions for this task. Click a suggested question below the message to ask it in the same chat.

If no skill was used, or the skill was edited or removed after the task was written, the chat shows the usual short intro instead.

### Example agent use case

An agent that manages design reviews might:

- Use the /prototype skill to indicate designs under review.
- In a comment, insert the prototype slug to surface the linked prototype card.
- Ready the prototype for quick, context‑appropriate opening by teammates.

### Keyboard workflow

Quickly assign or filter by skill using your keyboard:

- **Ctrl+K** — Command palette; start typing **"Skill"** to find:
  - **Skills** — Open Skill management.
  - **Filter tasks by skill** — Pop up the skill selector.

- Use the skill picker in a board or task detail to click or navigate with arrow keys to select skills.

### Data model (for integrators)

- **Scope** — `personal` | `project` | `team`.
- A skill on a board applies only when that board is opened.
- A project skill applies across all boards in that project.
- A team skill applies automatically to all boards that your team owns.

title: MCP tool keep-alive for SSE connections
description: Old-style AI tool SSE connections now receive periodic keep-alives and stay open cleanly instead of dropping after a short timeout. Integrated into the hypertask_tasks MCP tool so task queries can proceed without stutter.
---

Old-style AI tool connections use Server-Sent Events (/sse) through the MCP server. Previously, a quiet connection would drop after a short idle period. After this fix, the server sends a small keep-alive heartbeat every 60 seconds to keep the connection alive. The connection then closes cleanly after a primary soft timeout (about 13 minutes). This improved reliability lets agents run schedules with long idle windows without losing connection.

An additional behavior is enforced through the *Hypertask Tasks* MCP tool. Clients that ask for a single task by its number as plain text are now rejected with a clear error. This prevents crashes like the one logged in [HTPR-7205](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7205) and ensures tasks can only be fetched via a ticket identifier (e.g., ``t-123``).

**Updated:** 
- Hypertask Tasks MCP tool now rejects requests with plain text ticket numbers and returns a helpful error message.
- Old-style SSE connections stay open with periodic keep-alives and close cleanly when idle.
- References: [MCP Overview](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/overview/), [MCP workflows](https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/workflows/)

### Guided start after token login

```bash
hypertask login --token <token> --human
```

```text
Signed in as Claude Code (agent of Maria Lopez)
Board: Product Launch
https://app.hypertask.ai/project?id=9142

Next steps your agent can run now:
  1. See the board:          hypertask task list --project 9142
  2. Create a first task:    hypertask task create --project 9142 --title "My first task"
  3. Read the board rules:   hypertask project playbook 9142

Or just ask your agent: "What's on my Hypertask board?"
```

Token login checks the token right away. On success, it shows who you are signed in as and the newest board across all boards the token can see. A missing title falls back to the short name. The example above uses a fictional write agent and board.

The CLI prints the server's steps: read-only agents get two steps, list and playbook, with no create step. If no board is available, `--human` says "No board yet. Create one in your Hypertask web app."

JSON is the default output. It keeps `success`, `saved`, and `configPath`, and adds:

| Field | What it contains |
|-------|------------------|
| `signedInAs` | The signed-in identity, including `name`. |
| `board` | The board's `id`, `title`, and `url`. |
| `nextSteps` | The server's suggested steps (three for write agents, two for read-only agents, none without a board), each with a CLI `command`. |
| `moreBoards` | A hint to run `hypertask project list` when the token can see several boards. |

The CLI waits at most about 1.5 seconds for the guide. If it times out or fails because of a network or server error, login still saves the token. It returns the previous saved-token output without the guided start. Saving a token does not mean the check passed.

  --project <id>

  --clear-assignees
      Remove every assignee from the task
  --labels <list>
      Replace the ticket's entire label set. Repeatable/comma-separated for this call only. Does not append. An empty value clears every label. Use --add-label to keep existing labels.
  --clear-labels
      Remove every label from the task; cannot combine with --labels values, --add-label(s), or --remove-label(s)
  --add-labels <list>
      Comma-separated label names or IDs to add, keeping existing labels (repeatable; e.g. "QA")
  --add-label <list>
      Alias of --add-labels. Add labels without dropping the ones already on the ticket (repeatable).
  --remove-labels <list>
      Comma-separated label names or IDs to remove, keeping other labels (repeatable)
  --remove-label <list>
      Alias of --remove-labels. Remove labels without dropping the ones you did not name (repeatable).
  --parent-task <ref>
      Parent task: internal id or ticket ref (e.g. HTPR-4578)
  --clear-parent
      Detach this task from its parent
  --attach <path>
      Attach local file to task after update (repeatable)

Example:
  hypertask task update <ticket-or-task-id> --title <text>

  -h, --help
      Show help
